n: Ardbeg 10 year old, 46%
t: Floral aromas, along with peat smoke, lemon, pine needle, lime, green bell pepper, lobster pots, iodine,
f: Floral aromas, along with peat smoke, lemon, pine needle, lime, green bell pepper, lobster pots, iodine, smoky bacon chips, and hints of medicated soap. Sweet citrus, nippy spices, briny sea spray, butterscotch candy, and nutmeg on the palate, with a finish of espresso, smoke, and aniseed balls.

n: Virginia Distillery Co. The Brewer’s Coalition 4 Hands Brewing Co. Madagascar Stout Cask Finished, 50%
t: The malty, chocolate-driven nose points to the cask finish in play here—that of Madagascar stout barrels from
f: The malty, chocolate-driven nose points to the cask finish in play here—that of Madagascar stout barrels from St. Louis, Missouri’s 4 Hands Brewing Co. Marshmallow fluff, cocoa powder, and a bright pop of raspberry coulis create an incredibly alluring nose; these aromas transfer deftly to the palate, where there’s also some orange peel, candied ginger, and Black Forest cake. The finish ties everything up with a neat little bow, combining ground coffee, berry fruit, and chocolate.

n: Lost Lantern Single Cask Series Broad Branch Distilling 8 Year Old North Carolina Straight Rye, 70.8%
t: This single barrel from North Carolina’s Broad Branch Distilling, made from 100% Washington state prairie
f: This single barrel from North Carolina’s Broad Branch Distilling, made from 100% Washington state prairie rye, practically leaps out of the glass with punchy aromas of cinnamon powder, orange marmalade, clove, and spearmint gum. A lush mouthfeel pairs plenty of barrel influence with dark chocolate and heaps of spice. The eye-watering finish packs in even more notes of dark chocolate and spice—rye lovers will revel in this.

n: Oban 14 year old, 43%
t: This classic malt has a nose of marmalade on hot buttered toast, dabs of honey, sea breezes over sand dunes,
f: This classic malt has a nose of marmalade on hot buttered toast, dabs of honey, sea breezes over sand dunes, grapefruit peel, eucalyptus, dark chocolate, and seasoned oak. Rich and full-bodied with tangy citrus peels, honey, marmalade, lots of salinity, candied citrus, almonds, and malt. A dry finish of salt, citrus peel, and traces of honey.

n: Clynelish 14 year old, 46%
t: Bold, complex, and a benchmark Highland malt, the nose boasts roasted spices, orange blossom, beeswax,
f: Bold, complex, and a benchmark Highland malt, the nose boasts roasted spices, orange blossom, beeswax, snuffed candles, and vanilla fudge, with a pleasing coastal salinity. Opening with flavors of orange peel, malt, and sea salt, there’s a wave of spices ushering in the famous waxy mouthfeel, perhaps more pronounced than ever, getting creamier with Bramley apple peels, smoke, and spice, with a salty finish of sour apple candies.

n: Lost Lantern Single Cask Series New Riff Distilling Kentucky Straight Rye, 57.8%
t: Made from New Riff’s standard rye mashbill of 95% rye and 5% malted rye, this single cask is awash with
f: Made from New Riff’s standard rye mashbill of 95% rye and 5% malted rye, this single cask is awash with cinnamon applesauce, red fruit, citrus peel, and warming spice on the nose. A lovely array of flavors comes forth on the palate, among them baked apple, chocolate ice cream, toasted nuts, and spearmint gum. The finish is creamy and skews darker, with wood spice, black pepper, and a hint of char leading the way.

n: Lost Lantern Single Cask Series Montgomery Distillery, 52.3%
t: This comes at you with a haymaker nose of oak, barrel char, cherry cheesecake, chocolate-covered berries, and
f: This comes at you with a haymaker nose of oak, barrel char, cherry cheesecake, chocolate-covered berries, and Dr Pepper. The palate leads with more oak, peanut brittle, and chewy Chips Ahoy amid spices like cinnamon stick, chai, and pepper. The tannins recede on the finish, revealing black cherry, Ghirardelli dark chocolate, vanilla cream, and leather at the very end. Powerful from start to finish, but carries its proof very well.

n: Lost Lantern Single Cask Series Fiddler Soloist Georgia Straight Bourbon, 65%
t: Hailing from Georgia’s ASW Distillery, this is a 7 year old. The nose captures malt-heavy flavors: there’s
f: Hailing from Georgia’s ASW Distillery, this is a 7 year old. The nose captures malt-heavy flavors: there’s rich chocolate, Werther’s candies, and wood spice, as well as strawberry jam and torched orange. The palate is deliciously creamy and packed with wood influence, alongside an earthier note of anise. Pepper, barrel char, and baking spice round out the finish.

n: Bear Fight Kentucky Reserve Reposado Tequila Barrel Finished, 45%
t: The tequila cask influence is readily apparent in the aroma, as notes of cooked agave combine with vanilla
f: The tequila cask influence is readily apparent in the aroma, as notes of cooked agave combine with vanilla bean ice cream, toasted nuts, and a hint of raisin. A little key lime pie and black pepper on the palate are more evidence of the cask finish: Vanilla notes take a back seat, but they’re still there. The finish is short and citrusy sweet, leaving little to be desired, but overall pleasant, especially for the tequila fans among us.

n: Talisker 10 year old, 40%
t: Ground pepper spiciness balanced with sweetness, seaweed, squeezed orange quarters, and a hint of chile
f: Ground pepper spiciness balanced with sweetness, seaweed, squeezed orange quarters, and a hint of chile flakes, the peppery spices underpinned by peat smoke. This has more body and is a more rounded, mellow whisky than Talisker’s NAS expressions. Vanilla, green apple, citrus, punchy peppercorns, barley sugar, toffee, and smoke on the palate leave a comforting creamy finish with vanilla toffee, smoke, and pepper.

n: Dalwhinnie 15 year old, 43%
t: Not to be overlooked, this classic dram has a nose of honey, banana chip, malted barley, Cheerios, vanilla
f: Not to be overlooked, this classic dram has a nose of honey, banana chip, malted barley, Cheerios, vanilla ice cream, and toasted spices, with light smoke weaving between the bourbon cask flavors. Sweet-tasting heather honey, baked green apple, vanilla sponge, and pear; the flavors evolve, layering on caramel, cinnamon frosting, baked pastries, nutmeg, and black pepper. The finish is fruity, with pear, vanilla, and cinnamon.

n: Talisker Storm, 40%
t: The moderately peaty intensity on the first sniff blows over to reveal aromas of ground pepper, granola,
f: The moderately peaty intensity on the first sniff blows over to reveal aromas of ground pepper, granola, vanilla, caramel sauce, and sea spray. Flavors of apple, cracked black pepper, berries, vanilla, and toffee entertain the taste buds before a breakthrough of rich, creamy vanilla, salted caramel, and crushed almonds if you let it all play out. The drying, mouth-coating finish brings forth mellow peat smoke, toffee, and tingling pepperiness.

n: Lost Lantern Far Flung Bourbon IV Slow Proofed Blend of Straights, 60.4%
t: A blend of bourbons from Baltimore Spirits, Rich Grain Distilling, High Wire Distilling, SanTan Spirits,
f: A blend of bourbons from Baltimore Spirits, Rich Grain Distilling, High Wire Distilling, SanTan Spirits, Whiskey Acres Distilling Co., Still Austin, and Wollersheim Distillery. This “slow proof” expression was proofed down over a period of several weeks. Sweet bananas, custard, earthiness, and angel food cake fill the nose. Orange marmalade, raspberry, and vanilla on the palate. The finish is a bit dry but the oak is balanced by chocolate pastry, vanilla, and tobacco.

n: Green River Honey Finished, 46%
t: Green River added locally sourced raw honey directly into the barrel during aging. This nontraditional step
f: Green River added locally sourced raw honey directly into the barrel during aging. This nontraditional step results in an amber-hued spirit with the aroma of breakfast pastry with whipped cream and raspberries. It (unsurprisingly) has honey flavors, along with some peanut brittle, mixed berries, milk chocolate, and minerality. It finishes like a honey cough drop, along with Cracker Jacks, toasted vanilla, and pleasant tannins.

n: Jura 12 year old, 40%
t: Initially matured in bourbon barrels, this core expression was finished in oloroso sherry casks. On the nose,
f: Initially matured in bourbon barrels, this core expression was finished in oloroso sherry casks. On the nose, lofty stone fruit pops out, with juicy apricot mingling with raspberry jam and cinnamon stick. The palate is light, yet packs a peppery punch with notable citrus peel, chocolate syrup, and hazelnut. The finish comes and goes rather swiftly, but a kick of spice, chocolate, and more stone fruit are welcome flavors.

n: Lost Lantern Single Cask Series Dread River Distilling Co. Alabama Straight Bourbon, 70.9%
t: This 6 year old Alabama bourbon was distilled from 60% white corn, 30% winter wheat, and 10% malted barley.
f: This 6 year old Alabama bourbon was distilled from 60% white corn, 30% winter wheat, and 10% malted barley. The proof and barrel influence are apparent from the jump, with heady notes of char, chocolate, baking spice, raisin, red fruit, and cooked plums on the nose. The palate marches on in that same direction, with more barrel char and oak coating the mouth, joined by brighter red berry notes. Ultimately, that char may prove too intense for the faint of heart, but if you can handle the heat, there’s a whole lot of big flavor to enjoy here.

n: Isle of Skye 12 year old Double Smoke, 40%
t: On the nose, this blend lives up to its name, delivering a heady mix of pungent smoke—both campfire and
f: On the nose, this blend lives up to its name, delivering a heady mix of pungent smoke—both campfire and peat—with charred orchard fruits and a rubbery, medicinal quality. The palate, while still heavily smoky, shows more depth, with orange and lime mingling with iodine and warming cocoa. The finish is spicier with cinnamon and cloves amidst the smoke. While on the shorter side, the finish wraps up with stewed apples and pears, balancing sweet and smoky flavors.

n: Johnnie Walker 15 year old Green Label, 43%
t: Built around four key malts from Talisker, Linkwood, Cragganmore, and Caol Ila, the nose is malty, with apple
f: Built around four key malts from Talisker, Linkwood, Cragganmore, and Caol Ila, the nose is malty, with apple pie, raisins, toffee apples, bread crust, banana, vanilla, peppercorns, and gentle woodsmoke. Lively and refreshing on the palate, with green apple, malty caramel, peppery spice, smoke, whisky-soaked raisins, dried apricot, a drizzle of honey, and growing smokiness. The finish is deep and warming, featuring stewed fruits, oak spices, and burnt sugar.

n: Lost Lantern Single Cask Series Day’s Defile 10 year old, 77.2%
t: A wave of heat carries bright notes of baked peach, honeyed fruits, vanilla soft serve, Lemonheads, caramel
f: A wave of heat carries bright notes of baked peach, honeyed fruits, vanilla soft serve, Lemonheads, caramel candy, and whipped cream on the nose. The palate offers more peach, then apricot, lemongrass, chai spice, chocolate, and almond paste, all mingling with tiramisu on the finish. The proof is very strong, so water is your friend here, tempering the heat while unlocking hidden flavors of coffee beans and earth.

n: Cragganmore 12 year old, 40%,
t: A perfect dram to pour as an aperitif, this has an attractive nose of heather honey, ground spices, salted
f: A perfect dram to pour as an aperitif, this has an attractive nose of heather honey, ground spices, salted lemons, fragrant flowers, and vanilla buttercream. It’s clean and refreshing with honey, lemon zest, shortbread, and light pepper, followed by butter toffee sweetness, poached pear, and a hint of malt. A fudgy, creamy sweetness rolls on into the finish, with flashes of candied lemon.

n: Cragganmore Distillers Edition, 40%
t: Its double-maturation in port-seasoned American oak casks fills the senses with aromas of berries—notably
f: Its double-maturation in port-seasoned American oak casks fills the senses with aromas of berries—notably strawberry and black currant—plum, baking spice, fruitcake, and honeyed oak. The berries are more subtle on the palate, with maraschino cherry, plum jam, and toffee, then hints of gingersnaps, fruitcake, stewed tea, cinnamon bark, and fresh berries to finish, leaving the impression that the port casks are providing the dominant voice throughout.

n: Crater Lake, 40%
t: Distilled entirely from rye and aged for 2 years, this has a dry, grainy nose of pumpernickel, rye spice,
f: Distilled entirely from rye and aged for 2 years, this has a dry, grainy nose of pumpernickel, rye spice, bitter dark chocolate, wood shop, and chai. The palate is light and somewhat spiky with Red Hots, pickled ginger, and toasted grains. The finish adds cinnamon, lemon zest, oak, and subtle floral flavors. It has a decent foundation, but it would greatly benefit from longer aging.

n: Lost Lantern Far Flung Bourbon 100 Slow Proofed Blend of Straights, 50%
t: A blend of bourbons from the same distillers as Far Flung Bourbon IV, and also proofed down over a number of
f: A blend of bourbons from the same distillers as Far Flung Bourbon IV, and also proofed down over a number of weeks. The sweet nose offers honey, Juicy Fruit, marzipan, and fresh oak. Vanilla and coconut on the palate. A bit hot for its ABV, and the wood is somewhat overbearing. The finish offers pepper spice, vanilla, and peanut shells.

n: Lost Lantern Single Cask Series Copperworks Distilling, 60.3%
t: Distilled from five different malted barleys with varying roast levels, and aged 3 years in new oak. Soft
f: Distilled from five different malted barleys with varying roast levels, and aged 3 years in new oak. Soft vanilla, orange peel, passion fruit, chocolate, blueberry, and dusty oak on the nose. The palate is soft, round, and malty, and the whiskey carries its proof well. Pleasant waxiness overall, with breakfast cereal, spice, and blueberry pie on the palate. The finish is perhaps a bit dry, but the whiskey is solid.

n: GlenAllachie 35 year old 1990 Vintage, 50.2%
t: A cask strength expression combining oloroso and Pedro Ximénez sherry casks, toasted new Appalachian oak, and
f: A cask strength expression combining oloroso and Pedro Ximénez sherry casks, toasted new Appalachian oak, and new mizunara oak. Oriental spices, incense, and that new oak on the nose, plus stewed fruit, treacle, fig, raisin, tiffin, allspice, blackberry, and cocoa powder. It unspools milk chocolate, jellied fruits, baking spice, and ginger root flavors, adding red apple, black cherry, and pineapple, with a lengthy finish of bittersweet citrus, chocolate, and mizunara.

n: Nc’nean Huntress Malted Teacake, 48.5%
t: It’s the melting butter that hits your senses first, sliding over the hot teacake with aromas of cookie
f: It’s the melting butter that hits your senses first, sliding over the hot teacake with aromas of cookie dough, coconut, and strawberry jam. The creamy butteriness on the palate is sublime, showing fruit loaf, French vanilla, chopped citrus peel, cinnamon, orchard fruit, and muscovado sugar, culminating in a lip-smacking, creamy finish. Matured in bourbon, oloroso sherry, and shaved, toasted, and re-charred casks; this imaginative and evocative fermentation experiment included Belgian ale yeast.

n: Eagle Rare 30 year old, 50.5%
t: Eagle Rare’s oldest whiskey yet. The mellow nose exudes eucalyptus, orange peel, apricot, cinnamon, vanilla,
f: Eagle Rare’s oldest whiskey yet. The mellow nose exudes eucalyptus, orange peel, apricot, cinnamon, vanilla, and mellow aged oak, while the palate offers orange marmalade, maraschino cherries, baked plums, vanilla, and pepper spice. The texture is smooth, the flavors are rich and undiminished by age, and the oak is ever-present but by no means overdone. On the contrary, it exerts a gentle influence and lends complexity. A major achievement for ultra-aged American whiskey.

n: Copper & Cask 11 year old Small Batch Series (Batch 16), 58.1%,
t: This high-rye bourbon is sourced from an undisclosed Indiana distillery. It’s a spice bomb, with loads of
f: This high-rye bourbon is sourced from an undisclosed Indiana distillery. It’s a spice bomb, with loads of cinnamon, nutmeg, and allspice on the nose, as well as toasted almonds and vanilla ice cream. On the palate, more classic bourbon notes emerge, among them powdered sugar, raspberry jam, and even more baking spice, keeping a good thing going. All in all, this is a divine sipper that’s balanced and maintains mouthwatering flavors throughout.

n: Diageo Rare Series 33 year old Talisker 1992 Vintage, 60.1%
t: Matured in refill American and European oak casks and finished for over 20 years in amoroso-seasoned American
f: Matured in refill American and European oak casks and finished for over 20 years in amoroso-seasoned American oak hogs- heads, the nose has smoky bacon, maple syrup, driftwood, vanilla, pepper spice, and a briny coastal character. Rich caramel, vanilla, stone fruits, marmalade peels, and peppery spice; it’s got the mellowness of old Taliskers, with graham cracker, malt, and galia melon, and a dry finish of lingering fruitiness, peat smoke, and pepper.

n: Talisker 47 year old Magma, 48.8%
t: Finished for 4 months in new American oak casks toasted with volcanic rock from Skye, there are malty aromas,
f: Finished for 4 months in new American oak casks toasted with volcanic rock from Skye, there are malty aromas, salty sea air, dried peach and mango, honey, citrus zest, flowers, vanilla, banana chip, and gentle smoke. Creamy, salty, and citrusy on the palate, with chile flakes adding fire, then vanilla, cookie dough, chocolate chip, seasoned oak, green olive, and a slightly waxy finish with chile, menthol, and dry oak.

n: Old Pulteney 30 year old, 50.4%
t: A career-spanning expression for distillery manager Malcolm Waring, who distilled the spirit, filled the
f: A career-spanning expression for distillery manager Malcolm Waring, who distilled the spirit, filled the casks, and then bottled this 200th anniversary release. Aromas of chocolate orange, salted fudge, Bartlett pear, ground cumin, and orange twist. Rich citrus flavors, poached pears in red wine, summer red berries, and peppery spice, with cinnamon swirl, nutmeg, milk chocolate, vanilla pods, and leather. The thick-textured finish brings more cinnamon and nutmeg, plus dark chocolate and baked apple.

n: Old Pulteney 50 year old, 40.8%
t: This golden anniversary release combines four American oak casks of 50 year old single malts. Coastal
f: This golden anniversary release combines four American oak casks of 50 year old single malts. Coastal minerality on the nose, with Honey Nut Cheerios, seasoned oak, grated nutmeg, golden sultana, tobacco, cigar box, cinnamon stick, and Sachertorte. This gentle dram offers flavors of citrus peel, dark chocolate, oak tannins, and black cherry, with hints of salt and spice before a long finish with more citrus juiciness and vanilla essence. Delicate yet decadent.

n: Nikka from the Barrel Malt Pieces of the Barrel 40th Anniversary Limited Edition, 58%,
t: A fascinating sub-blend of Nikka from the Barrel bottled at the blender’s preferred strength using
f: A fascinating sub-blend of Nikka from the Barrel bottled at the blender’s preferred strength using non-peated, lightly peated, and heavily peated stock from Nikka’s three malt distilleries with a core of Miyagikyo. Roasted nut, malt, honey, and toasted granola aromas, with a peated base, ashy smoke, baked lemon, golden raisin, and creamy vanilla. Maple syrup, vanilla extract, and nutty flavors are balanced by clove, cigar smoke, apple cake, cinnamon, and nutmeg. (800 sets of three 500ml bottles, including Nikka from the Barrel Extra Marriage, released last year, and Grain Pieces). $400/3 500ml bottle set

n: Miyagikyo 10 year old, 45%
t: Fruity, floral, sweet, and fresh, the nose has bright citrus and fresh orchard fruit, toasted marshmallow,
f: Fruity, floral, sweet, and fresh, the nose has bright citrus and fresh orchard fruit, toasted marshmallow, jasmine, Love Hearts, incense, perfume, and complex florals. This triumphs over previous versions; it’s refreshing, with baked apple, peach, nectarine, and pineapple, developing into marmalade, candied orange, and a fine spiciness, then almond, cherry cake, soft oak, and clove. The finish is waxy and sappy, with caramel and baked fruit.

n: Rare Character Limited Release Straight (Batch 2; 2026), 69.9%
t: On the nose, this commands attention, with bold aromas of fudge, cigar tobacco, berry jam, and seasoned oak.
f: On the nose, this commands attention, with bold aromas of fudge, cigar tobacco, berry jam, and seasoned oak. A swirl deepens the aromas, bringing out cherries, strawberry hard candies, and almond cookies. The sip is full-bodied and viscous with flavors of cherry cough drops, caramel latte, and burnt earth. With time, oak emerges as a dominant flavor mixed with fruit sweetness and maple syrup. The finish lingers, balancing bitter char with caramel sweetness.

n: New Riff 10 year old High Note Collection, 58.45%
t: This opens with a nose of antique shop, dark chocolate, cigar tobacco, blackberry jam, strawberry syrup,
f: This opens with a nose of antique shop, dark chocolate, cigar tobacco, blackberry jam, strawberry syrup, French vanilla, and a touch of banana pudding. Decadent chocolate shows up on the palate, expressed as fudge and Nesquik amid mocha and more straw- berry. The finish goes even darker and sweeter with malted milkshake, chocolate cake, and dark berries. The creamy texture and excellent integration make this a very hard dram to put down.

n: Russell’s Reserve 13 year old Barrel Proof (Spring 2026 Release), 60.6%
t: This milestone release has an explosive personality that comes out swinging with a seductive nose of dark
f: This milestone release has an explosive personality that comes out swinging with a seductive nose of dark chocolate, black cherry, car leather, butterscotch, cola, ground cinnamon, and charred oak. The palate follows suit with fudge, double chocolate-chip cookies, raspberry jam, caramel, spice, and dark-roast coffee. Cinnamon and nutmeg come to the fore on the finish, bringing even darker notes of leather, cocoa, and affogato al caffè, all perfectly framed by the oak.

n: Elijah Craig 15 year old Single Barrel (No. 372), 54%
t: It lures you in with aromas of rich vanilla, toasted almonds, marzipan, butterscotch, oak, cherries, and a
f: It lures you in with aromas of rich vanilla, toasted almonds, marzipan, butterscotch, oak, cherries, and a bit of coconut patty. The palate melds spicier flavors like cinnamon swirl ice cream, snickerdoodles, and spiced cherry preserves with strawberry jam, fudge, choco- late lava cake, and vanilla pudding. The intense finish brings cherries, blackberries, barrel spice, glove leather, and more chocolate. Excellent balance and integration throughout, carrying its high proof with grace.

n: Barrell Cigar Blend Madeira, Armagnac, Rum, and Hungarian Oak Cask Finished, 55.6%
t: Barrell’s take on a cigar blend is a beauty. The nose kicks off with fruity aromas of grape, ripe berries,
f: Barrell’s take on a cigar blend is a beauty. The nose kicks off with fruity aromas of grape, ripe berries, and black raspberry jam, but there’s plenty of baking spice too. On the palate, more berry fruit and cherry are joined by heaps of well-integrated chocolate and a hint of tobacco. The finish brings in Black Forest cake alongside persistent baking spice and berries—it’s a joy from start to finish.

n: Johnnie Walker Blue Label Azure, 43%
t: Master blender Dr. Emma Walker’s coastal-inspired take on Blue Label is crafted to complement seafood. The
f: Master blender Dr. Emma Walker’s coastal-inspired take on Blue Label is crafted to complement seafood. The nose brings sea salt, toffee pudding, citrus zest, maple syrup, dried apple, and delicate peat smoke. Creamy milk chocolate and maple syrup melt into molasses, toasted hazelnuts, bananas Foster, s’mores, vanilla, dried fruit, and soft peat smoke, with caramel, chile flakes, and warming spice carrying the finish. (Travel Retail exclusive)

n: Glenglassaugh 15 year old, 46%
t: The nose is almost Christmasy, with raisins, plum pudding, dried cranberries, sangria, and pine cone, plus
f: The nose is almost Christmasy, with raisins, plum pudding, dried cranberries, sangria, and pine cone, plus undertones of gingerbread and graham cracker. The compelling palate has wine-soaked tropical fruits, sea salt, Medjool dates, prune juice, dried apricots, and plenty of Christmas spice. That spice really intensifies on the finish, also bringing black currant, grape, and grilled pineapple. Deep and complex: A must-try for lovers of traditional sherried scotch.

n: GlenAllachie 19 year old Masters of Wood Ex-Solera Sherry Cask Matured, 50%
t: Matured in bourbon barrels, then finished in casks used for 55 years in an oloroso and PX sherry solera
f: Matured in bourbon barrels, then finished in casks used for 55 years in an oloroso and PX sherry solera system. Indulgent aromas of plum jam, cocoa-dusted truffles, vanilla pod, cacao nibs, espresso, heather honey, and caramel sauce. It’s a superb expression for sherry lovers, with flavors of plum, marmalade, old armagnac, treacle buns, fruity black coffee, gingerbread, and chocolate brownie, and a finish of cocoa, ginger, and plum.

n: Isle of Harris, 46%
t: Matured in first-fill bourbon and oloroso sherry casks, this exudes a balanced combination of saltiness,
f: Matured in first-fill bourbon and oloroso sherry casks, this exudes a balanced combination of saltiness, sweetness, and creaminess. Fresh coastal breezes, honey, vanilla, light peat smoke, custard creams, butterscotch, banana, and seaweed aromas abound. The thick, mouth-coating texture presents flavors of butterscotch sauce, lemon curd, lime zest, kiwi, gooseberry, crème brûlée, pink grapefruit, and sour cherries. The finish brings butterscotch over melon balls, peppery spice, and a blast of peat smoke. This really stands out.

n: Little Book Chapter 10: “All the Wiser” Sherry and Toasted Bourbon Cask Finished, 61.3%
t: This greets you with sweet and powerful aromas of melted caramel, toasted marshmal- low, cherrywood, vanilla
f: This greets you with sweet and powerful aromas of melted caramel, toasted marshmal- low, cherrywood, vanilla bean, and cinnamon sugar. Chocolate lovers should brace them- selves before sipping, as Fudgsicle and chewy double chocolate-chip cookie lead the palate, along with oak, warming cinnamon, nutmeg, cherry, and chopped peanuts. Even more chocolate emerges on the long and complex finish, joined by vanilla milkshake, leather, black cherry, and subtle baking spice.

n: Glenmorangie X Harrison Ford, 46.5%
t: This rebellious Glenmorangie has bite, thanks to whisky finished in toasted Portuguese red wine casks. The
f: This rebellious Glenmorangie has bite, thanks to whisky finished in toasted Portuguese red wine casks. The nose raids the senses with ruby grapefruit, orange oils, perfumed florals, dried stone fruits, rose Turkish delight, tart cranberry, and marzipan. Grapefruit marmalade flavors crack the whip with thick peel, sweet orange, pepper, aniseed, and menthol lozenges, leaving a mouth-coating finish like tears in the rain, with citrus oils, brown sugar sweetness, and supple oak.

n: Laphroaig 15 year old, 46%
t: Making a permanent return after being discontinued in 2009, the complex nose boasts sea salt, creosote, hot
f: Making a permanent return after being discontinued in 2009, the complex nose boasts sea salt, creosote, hot asphalt, seaweed, vanilla cream, balsa wood, antiseptics, ground almond, Band-Aids, sanded oak, zested lemon, and rubber. Creamy lemon mousse, grapefruit, chile powder, clove, cinnamon, crushed fennel, and tarragon, with stone fruits emerging from under the blanket of spices, though the finish remains intensely spicy. Rejoice! Hardcore Laphroaig is back!

n: Elijah Craig PGA Championship Commemorative Edition (2026 Release), 54%
t: Heaven Hill’s annual release to commemorate this PGA major. Mellow jammy red fruit, vanilla custard, and soft
f: Heaven Hill’s annual release to commemorate this PGA major. Mellow jammy red fruit, vanilla custard, and soft grain fill the nose. The palate is lush with grape jelly, blueberry, and vanilla. On the mellow, more jammy red fruit appears, providing great depth of flavor. This is an excellent bourbon, with balance and great flavor development.

n: Laphroaig Willem Dafoe, 53.7%
t: Finished in oloroso casks, Dafoe’s dram evokes strong memories of a seaside summer cookout, with grill smoke,
f: Finished in oloroso casks, Dafoe’s dram evokes strong memories of a seaside summer cookout, with grill smoke, brisket, oyster shells, and sea salt, alongside baked berries, torched brown sugar, caramel, and a hint of marmalade on the nose. The palate is rich with burnt ends, pork belly, espresso, tiramisu, Whoppers, and more mouthwatering smoke. These flavors linger on the long finish, which gracefully fades out on a very pleasant mesquite barbecue flavor.

n: Barrell Cask Strength Blend (Batch 038), 58.48%
t: This blend of bourbons aged between 8 and 15 years was distilled in Kentucky, Indiana, Tennessee, and
f: This blend of bourbons aged between 8 and 15 years was distilled in Kentucky, Indiana, Tennessee, and Maryland. The nose balances youth and maturity, with bright fruits tempered by dusty leather and well-worn oak. The palate opens with sweetened cereal grains and a hint of marshmallow. Water draws out apricot and apples. With time, it turns more savory with chicory, walnuts, and dried herbs. The finish is exceptionally long with seasoned oak and more leather.

n: Booker’s “Big Easy Batch” 7 year old (2026-01), 64.55%
t: This pays homage to New Orleans, which was one of Booker Noe’s favorite cities to visit. From the start, it’s
f: This pays homage to New Orleans, which was one of Booker Noe’s favorite cities to visit. From the start, it’s a bourbon lover’s dream—a warming and well-spiced nose invites you back for more, where caramel, vanilla, raisin, confectionary sugar, strawberry jam, and dried fruit linger. The palate is searingly hot, but underneath that heat there’s a lot to love, including dark chocolate, barrel char, black coffee, and more dark dried fruit. Chocolate ganache, espresso, and truffle emerge on the finish, making this a big bourbon befitting the Big Easy.

n: Diageo Rare Series 55 year old Glenury Royal 1970 Vintage, 62.4%
t: Initially matured in American oak hogsheads, then married in European oak puncheons, this has aromas of
f: Initially matured in American oak hogsheads, then married in European oak puncheons, this has aromas of antique wood, vintage bookshop, honeysuckle, dry oak, banana chip, and white pepper, opening up to more fruitiness of pear, crisp green apple, and apple pie. Sweet, creamy, and succulent on the palate, with honey, apple, cinder toffee, and banana custard, then peach, nutmeg, malt, and a dollop of vanilla ice cream on a thick, creamy finish.

n: Daniel Weller Spelt Wheat, 47%
t: The second whiskey in the Daniel Weller series, known for its experimental releases. This uses spelt, a
f: The second whiskey in the Daniel Weller series, known for its experimental releases. This uses spelt, a species of wheat, in place of rye in the mashbill, and is aged 10 years. Honey, maple syrup, and clove create a Christmasy nose, The palate is full of coconut, vanilla, and dried herbs, with a finish that is somewhat dry. Powerful but well balanced, with sweet flavors bursting through.

n: Diageo Rare Series 34 year old Blair Athol 1991 Vintage, 50.8%
t: Matured in refill European oak casks and finished in Pedro Ximénez-seasoned new American oak hogsheads, this
f: Matured in refill European oak casks and finished in Pedro Ximénez-seasoned new American oak hogsheads, this is bone-dry on the nose with chestnut puree, dark chocolate, coffee creams, fig roll, and fine oak spices. Quite delicious, with sweetened chocolate fondant cake, raspberry jam, hazelnut praline paste, and gentle peppercorn spiciness, plus hints of espresso and black cherry. A drying finish of supple oak, wood spices, and coffee cake.

n: Kilchoman 14 year old Family Collection Rockside Bourbon Cask, 50.9%
t: A combination of honey, vanilla, fondant cream, coconut strips, peat smoke, and alluringly salty green olives
f: A combination of honey, vanilla, fondant cream, coconut strips, peat smoke, and alluringly salty green olives on the nose. A delicious palate of vanilla, malt, peel oil, clove, and pepper subsides to sweet fudge, tangy fruit, and candied citrus, rounding off with banana custard and creamy malt ushering in a silky finish of vanilla and nectarine.

n: Glenmorangie The Thirty, 43%
t: This combines a parcel finished in Burgundy red wine casks with bourbon cask-matured stock. The aromas are
f: This combines a parcel finished in Burgundy red wine casks with bourbon cask-matured stock. The aromas are luxurious, showing plum, raspberry, vanilla extract, dark choco- late, nutmeg, and Luxardo cherry syrup. Velvety textured and weighty, with maraschino cherry, dark vanilla, fresh fig, plum, black currant, and melted chocolate. The oak influence towers over the finish, bringing wood spices, citrus peel, leather, cocoa, and a gentle pepperiness.

n: Kilchoman 11 year old Family Collection Sherry Butts, 54.7%
t: The nose has chopped orange peel, dried vine fruit, allspice, star anise, dried fig, leather, and breezy peat
f: The nose has chopped orange peel, dried vine fruit, allspice, star anise, dried fig, leather, and breezy peat smoke. Water cools the spice heat, but neat, there’s candied orange, dates, pepper, clove, peat smoke, roasted nuts, gingerbread, dark chocolate, oak char, and dark soy sauce, with a finish of burnt oak, dark chocolate- covered ginger, and peat fires.

n: Barrell 21 year old Toasted Single Barrel Extra Strength, 62.2%
t: This ultra-aged blend features bourbons distilled in Kentucky, Indiana, and Tennessee that are finished in
f: This ultra-aged blend features bourbons distilled in Kentucky, Indiana, and Tennessee that are finished in toasted American oak. There’s a great deal of earthiness on the nose— Moroccan mint tea, pine needle, anise, and lemon peel—plus vanilla bean and a crack of black pepper. A lovely mouthfeel is accompanied by sweeter notes of toasted marshmallow, Nutella, hot fudge, dried fruit, and gingersnaps. The finish leans into cinnamon, evoking frosted cinnamon bun and a bit of tobacco leaf. A delicious complex sipper!

n: Diageo Rare Series 42 year old Caol Ila 1983 Vintage, 56.4%
t: Initially matured in refill American oak hogsheads and married in European oak puncheons, the glass exudes
f: Initially matured in refill American oak hogsheads and married in European oak puncheons, the glass exudes sweet peat smoke and peaty fun, lemon cheesecake, toasted oak, spicy meat rubs, and pink peppercorn aromas. It’s an intense flavor experience with sweet citrus, smoke, and a burst of citrus peel, while water releases menthol, vanilla toffee, pineapple, and more tropical fruits, leaving a creamy sweet, smoky finish.

n: Bernheim 10 year old 20th Anniversary, 57.3%
t: Aromas of warm baking spice, plentiful vanilla, pancakes, butter, and maple syrup fill the nose. Loads of
f: Aromas of warm baking spice, plentiful vanilla, pancakes, butter, and maple syrup fill the nose. Loads of breakfast and bakery flavors are accented by pepper spice, raspberry jam, chocolate, and vanilla. The long, smooth finish serves up more vanilla and spice. Despite the proof, it’s so delicate, flavorful, smooth, and delicious.

n: Kilchoman Maury Cask Matured, 50%
t: Maury is a sweet fortified wine made in France’s Roussillon region. This was not finished in Maury casks—it
f: Maury is a sweet fortified wine made in France’s Roussillon region. This was not finished in Maury casks—it was fully matured in them, a first for Kilchoman. The aroma is oddly sweet, while a sip brings a mix of blackberry jam, dark chocolate, candied yams and Cuban coffee, loaded with enough sugar to make the spoon stand in the cup. Water brings out more coffee, with a touch of mocha and savory peat smoke. Sweet, rich, and memorable.

n: Rare Character Limited Release (Batch 1; 2026), 59.47%
t: This exceptional rye delivers depth and complexity. The nose is resplendent with mint, fennel, cloves, and
f: This exceptional rye delivers depth and complexity. The nose is resplendent with mint, fennel, cloves, and spiced vanilla. The palate is bold with balanced sweetness; white pepper, thyme, and sweet mint, all fleshed out by sweeter flavors of apple, raisin, and candied pecans. The finish is long and spicy, with dried herbs and oak.

n: Dingle 10 year old, 46.5%
t: This was matured in a ratio of 65% bourbon, 30% port, and 5% PX sherry casks. The aromas swirl with cherry,
f: This was matured in a ratio of 65% bourbon, 30% port, and 5% PX sherry casks. The aromas swirl with cherry, plum, blackened spices, Red Vines, marmalade peel, cookie dough, and ripe cantaloupe. Layers of flavor and complexity on the palate, with strawberry, clove, gentle oak, and smooth caramel kept in check by a tart port character. Dark chocolate on the finish, with hints of blackened oak.

n: Blue Run Blueprint Series, 52.5%
t: For this inaugural Blueprint bourbon, Blue Run combined two mashbills, one wheated, the other comprised of
f: For this inaugural Blueprint bourbon, Blue Run combined two mashbills, one wheated, the other comprised of 80% corn, 15% rye, and 5% malted barley. The nose is a touch reticent and slightly musty, yielding Ovaltine, sugar cookie, simple syrup, and chocolate-covered strawberries. Much more chocolate arrives on the palate, though there’s also a pop of black pepper, pound cake, and red fruit. Chocolate crinkle cookies and berry fruit combine for an alluring finish.

n: Lost Lantern Single Cask Series Boulder Spirits 7 year old, 69.4%
t: A vibrant unpeated single malt with a bold sense of Colorado terroir. The aromatic nose offers fresh
f: A vibrant unpeated single malt with a bold sense of Colorado terroir. The aromatic nose offers fresh grain—bushels of it—plus licorice, coffee, oak spice, and dark chocolate. The palate is deliciously sweet, with apricot, vanilla, peach, and raspberry coulis, anchored by earthy flavors, clove, and pepper spice. The finish is long, complex, and spicy with specks of maple syrup and caffe latte sweetness, balanced against bitter oak. Good integration between the bitter and the sweet; harmonious with plenty of boldness.

n: Blue Note Special Reserve Cask Finished Series Blend of Straights (2026 Release), 59.5%
t: From nose to finish, this is dense but never overly crowded, skillfully balancing the influence of the
f: From nose to finish, this is dense but never overly crowded, skillfully balancing the influence of the cognac, vanilla cognac, madeira, sherry, port, vino de naranja, apricot brandy, and winter bock finishing casks. On the nose, there’s salted caramel, glazed doughnuts, blueberry syrup, and toasted graham cracker. The sweet aromas carry over to the lively palate, accented by pepper and oak. As it develops in the glass, rye spice and sweet mint—reminiscent of a Julep—come to the forefront. The finish balances charred oak with cinnamon candy sweetness.

n: Barrell 12 year old French Oak Cask Finished Blend, 56.7%
t: A blend of bourbons sourced from Kentucky, Indiana, Tennessee, and Wyoming, all aged 12 to 15 years, this
f: A blend of bourbons sourced from Kentucky, Indiana, Tennessee, and Wyoming, all aged 12 to 15 years, this whiskey’s French oak finish is the star of the show. Heady baking spice, vanilla, strawberry jam, clove, and caramel pull you into the glass. Despite being higher proof, the palate is silky smooth, draped with spice, vanilla icing, cooked cherries, toasted marshmallow, and Heath bar. More of the same on the finish, as gooey toasted marsh- mallow melds with vanilla, barrel char, and a hint of black pepper.

n: First West Explorer Baby Black Corn, 47.5%
t: The nose offers ginger, dried herbs, generous cinnamon spice, caramel, baked apple, vanilla, and barrel char,
f: The nose offers ginger, dried herbs, generous cinnamon spice, caramel, baked apple, vanilla, and barrel char, leading to a mellow, smooth palate brimming with nutmeg, almond, and vanilla-coconut ice cream. Warm and full on a loaded finish of chocolate, spice, and peanuts, plus the flavors of the palate. There’s a halo of mellowed sweetness overall, then this one just keeps on coming with excellent follow-through. Well balanced and delicious.

n: Stranahan’s Peated Cask (Batch 10), 45%
t: After aging in new American oak, this was finished in peated whisky casks from Islay and the U.S. On the
f: After aging in new American oak, this was finished in peated whisky casks from Islay and the U.S. On the nose, the peated casks’ influence is immediately evident, with smoke and spice mixing with tropical fruit and caramel candies. The palate is charred and grilled, with wood smoke, burnt grains, hay, and Reese’s Peanut Butter Cups creating layers of flavor. The finish balances sweet and bitter exceptionally, with milk chocolate and ashy smoke.

n: Sailor’s Home Journey, 43%
t: This triple-distilled, triple cask blend of grain and malt whiskeys is matured in virgin American oak and
f: This triple-distilled, triple cask blend of grain and malt whiskeys is matured in virgin American oak and bourbon barrels, then finished in Jamaican rum casks. The aromas are dark, sweet, and syrupy, with butterscotch, rum babka, bananas Foster, cinnamon bun, and toasted oak. Light-bodied, with delicious flavors of Caribbean black cake, treacle sponge, melted toffee, brandy snaps, and malted milk, with a finish of vanilla extract and rum-raisin.

n: Old Grand-Dad 114 Single Barrel (Lot 001), 57%
t: Nutty and bold on the nose; it’s approachable despite its high proof. With a swirl in the glass, peanuts,
f: Nutty and bold on the nose; it’s approachable despite its high proof. With a swirl in the glass, peanuts, almonds, and pecans mix with vanilla frosting, fudge, and cloves, creating a warm, welcoming aroma. On the palate, the nuttiness sweetens with waves of vanilla bean, caramel apple, and marzipan. The finish shows a hint of the higher proof and lasts long with cinnamon spice and faint oak.

n: Dalmore Regalis, 43%
t: Brown sugar, treacle, toffee, and mulled wine on the nose. The palate has a pleasant creamy texture, with
f: Brown sugar, treacle, toffee, and mulled wine on the nose. The palate has a pleasant creamy texture, with caramel, chocolate, stewed plums, a hint of rancio, and baked berries; a heavily sherried profile overall. The finish offers chocolate, well-aged oak, graphite, cocoa powder, and baked berries. There is a deftness to the whisky’s flavor profile, helping to overcome a finish that’s just a bit overdone.

n: Dewar’s 19 year old The Champion’s Edition (2026 Release), 43%
t: Cabernet Franc red wine casks from near New York’s Shinnecock Hills Golf Club, host of this year’s U.S. Open,
f: Cabernet Franc red wine casks from near New York’s Shinnecock Hills Golf Club, host of this year’s U.S. Open, wrap this year’s edition in silky elegance. It tees off with aromas of plum, red cherry, fragrant violet fondant creams, seasoned oak, nutmeg, and sugar-sprinkled honey cookies. Even smoother than the 2025 release, it’s a well-balanced combination of cherry, berry fruit, caramel, peppery spice, citrus peel, cinnamon, and Brazil nut, leaving a rich, lingering, fruity sweetness.

n: The ImpEx Collection 14 year old 2011 Vintage Burnside Chateau Latour Barrique (No. 24789), 63.8%
t: Finishing scotch in a wine barrel isn’t a novel concept, but doing so in a cask that once held a first-growth
f: Finishing scotch in a wine barrel isn’t a novel concept, but doing so in a cask that once held a first-growth Bordeaux takes the idea to a different level. This has an extremely dark color that’s reminiscent of cola, with an earthy nose that also has guava, kiwi, and other tropical fruits. The first sip rewards you with sweetness—toasted pralines and baked apples call you in—followed by chocolate that lasts through the finish.

n: Chivas Regal 16 year old Charles Leclerc, 40%
t: Using Longmorn as the key malt, this 16-component blend was inspired by the Ferrari driver’s F1 racing
f: Using Longmorn as the key malt, this 16-component blend was inspired by the Ferrari driver’s F1 racing number. The nose offers red apples, thick marmalade peels, peppercorn, strawberry sorbet, summer red berries, and toasted oak. The palate brings toffee, malt, dried fruits, red cherry, ginger root, cinnamon, pineapple, and grapefruit peel, concluding with a bitter- sweet citrus finish.

n: Isle of Raasay Hungarian Oak, 50%
t: Fully matured in tight-grained Hungarian oak oloroso sherry casks, the nose revels in marmalade, crystallized
f: Fully matured in tight-grained Hungarian oak oloroso sherry casks, the nose revels in marmalade, crystallized ginger, cinnamon, roasted spices, barbecue smoke, and a hint of menthol. Roasted chestnut and cacao nib aromas emerge later. This drinks beautifully without water, showing gingersnaps, marmalade, walnuts, dark chocolate, coffee bean, and light peat smoke. The nose and palate correlate closely, wrapping up with a finish of spicy smoke and chocolate orange.

n: Blue Note Wheated, 50.5%
t: A wheater from the often-over- looked B.R. Distilling in Memphis. Soft on the nose, with cinnamon roll,
f: A wheater from the often-over- looked B.R. Distilling in Memphis. Soft on the nose, with cinnamon roll, candied orange, lemon spritz, unripe pears, apple orchard, polished oak, honey, varnish, and earthiness. The palate offers vanilla, savory spice, cinnamon, fresh bread, pepper spice, toffee, and peach pie. Nicely textured, with a delicious finish of lemon and honey. Creamy and delicious overall, with a pleasant softness throughout.

n: Berry Bros. & Rudd Knockdhu 2012 Vintage Single Cask (No. 7127), 58.8%
t: This vintage-dated Highland single malt is delightfully fruity on the nose, opening with ripe banana, toasted
f: This vintage-dated Highland single malt is delightfully fruity on the nose, opening with ripe banana, toasted nuts, a little mustiness, and light spice. The palate cranks up the spice, but the heat is never overwhelming, leading to hazelnut, chocolate, and dried fruit. Fruit, nuts, coffee, and chocolate meld into a lengthy finish.

n: Diageo Rare Series 42 year old Clynelish 1983 Vintage, 49.5%
t: Fully matured in American oak hogsheads, this stately dram has aromas of golden syrup cake, nutmeg, cinnamon,
f: Fully matured in American oak hogsheads, this stately dram has aromas of golden syrup cake, nutmeg, cinnamon, and lavender soap. Easy to drink neat, the well-rounded palate embodies the renowned Clynelish waxy texture, with flavors of caramel, heather honey, chile flakes, white pepper, mustard seed, vanilla, dark chocolate, and a hint of dill pickle. A mouth-coating finish serves up salted caramel, dark chocolate, and lingering spice.

n: Kilchoman 20 year old Family Collection Bourbon Cask, 49.9%
t: Vibrant tropical fruitiness on the nose—think lemon zest, star fruit, cantaloupe, and guava—plus vanilla
f: Vibrant tropical fruitiness on the nose—think lemon zest, star fruit, cantaloupe, and guava—plus vanilla fudge, honeycomb, lemon drops, polished oak, and soft, well-integrated peat smoke. With sweet fruit flavors of hard candies and dried orange, it develops a rich, viscous mouthfeel with marmalade and panna cotta, ending with lime zest, kiwi, and gooseberry fool. A mouth-coating finish brings lime curd and drying oak.

n: Kilchoman 18 year old Family Collection Bourbon Cask, 50%
t: The nose is incredibly soft, with apple pie filling, grilled pineapple, vanilla cream, peach, heather honey,
f: The nose is incredibly soft, with apple pie filling, grilled pineapple, vanilla cream, peach, heather honey, fading peat smoke, oak shavings, and a hint of cinnamon breakfast cereal. Quietly elegant, with flavors of Seville orange peel, baked pastries, and a spritz of sea spray followed by apricot jam, walnut, and malted milk. A long-lingering finish of baked fruit, lemon peel, and salt crystals follows.

n: Kilchoman 10 year old Loch Gorm Sherry Cask Matured (2026 Release), 46%
t: This annual limited offering from Kilchoman marries peat and sherry funk, balancing sweet and inviting
f: This annual limited offering from Kilchoman marries peat and sherry funk, balancing sweet and inviting flavors with a hint of wildness. On the nose, plenty of peat meets overripe berries, grilled pineapple, and honey, balancing the smoky, earthy aromas. The palate dials back the smoke and reveals milk chocolate, citrus, French toast, and tart and funky red fruits. The finish brings peat and sweet in almost equal measure with cinnamon sugar and earthy smoke.

n: Nikka from the Barrel Grain Pieces of the Barrel 40th Anniversary Limited Edition, 58%
t: The sweet, rounded component of Nikka from the Barrel uses both mature and young Coffey grain whisky from
f: The sweet, rounded component of Nikka from the Barrel uses both mature and young Coffey grain whisky from Miyagikyo, blended with a corn and rye grain whisky from Satsumatsukasa Distillery in Kyushu. Creamy vanilla, fresh coconut, cornbread, honey, lychee, white flowers, and fresh linen aromas. Those initial honey and corn aromas carry through on the palate along with tangy orange sherbet, almond, gingerbread, and toasted coconut, while water adds richness and darker syrupy tones. (800 sets of three 500 ml bottles, including Nikka From the Barrel Extra Marriage, released last year, and Malt Pieces). $400/3 500ml bottle set

n: GlenAllachie 10 year old 2015 Vintage America 250 Mizunara Hogshead Single Cask (No. 1951), 60.4%
t: This opulent malt opens with a nose overflowing with vanilla custard, banana pudding, and freshly baked
f: This opulent malt opens with a nose overflowing with vanilla custard, banana pudding, and freshly baked brownies. The palate is more complex, with toffee and peanut brittle adding depth and additional sweetness. With water, oak and spice emerge, along with baking chocolate, cinnamon, and toasted grains. While this takes water well, it remains quite approachable even at bottling strength. The finish offers brown sugar sweetness and polished oak.

n: Virginia Distillery Co. The Brewer’s Coalition North Coast Brewing Co. Old Rasputin Russian Imperial Stout Cask Finished, 50%
t: This limited edition is finished in barrels that once held North Coast’s Old Rasputin stout. It invites you
f: This limited edition is finished in barrels that once held North Coast’s Old Rasputin stout. It invites you in with a chocolaty aroma that cloaks subtler notes of blackberry, strawberry rhubarb, and vanilla. The spicy, multifaceted palate has a deep stout-like maltiness, hazelnut spread, plum pudding, fruitcake, and a hint of Mexican hot chocolate. There’s some jalapeño zing on the finish accompanied by even more chocolate. Pleasantly complex and spicy.

n: Virginia Distillery Co. 7 year old First Cut Cigar Blend, 54%
t: Aged in a panoply of casks including Spanish oak, sherry, port, STR, cabernet, armagnac, cognac, and fino, it
f: Aged in a panoply of casks including Spanish oak, sherry, port, STR, cabernet, armagnac, cognac, and fino, it has inviting aromas of mixed nuts, double chocolate muffin, straw- berry, and toasted almond. The sherry makes itself known on the palate, offering dried cranberries, wine-soaked fruits, and chocolate- covered cherries, plums, and raisins. The finish evolves, with barrel spice, dark fruit, and brighter stone fruit joining the party. Surprisingly well-integrated considering all the barrels in play.

n: Remus Master Distiller Experimental Series No. 2 2017 Vintage Tawny Port, White Port, Oloroso Sherry, and Ruby Port Cask Finished Straight, 56.5%
t: Remus brand’s first wheat whiskey is bright and fruity on the nose with an inviting blend of raspberry,
f: Remus brand’s first wheat whiskey is bright and fruity on the nose with an inviting blend of raspberry, cherry, and grape jelly. The palate is sweet, too, but more confectionary with chocolate chips, honey buns, and fruit tarts. With time, it shows excellent evolution with charred oak, dark chocolate, and a hint of sour cherry tempering the sweet flavors. The finish is long and full of oak and dried fruit, creating a delightfully cohesive sip.

n: Bernheim Barrel Proof (Batch A226), 62%
t: Vanilla sherbet, waffle cone, caramel, chopped walnuts, toasted almond, and black cherry drizzle characterize
f: Vanilla sherbet, waffle cone, caramel, chopped walnuts, toasted almond, and black cherry drizzle characterize a nose reminis- cent of an ice cream shop. It’s a bit fruitier on the palate, offering cherry pie, raspberry coulis, powdered sugar, chocolate sprinkles, and a bit of peppery heat from the proof. The finish adds blackberry cobbler, spiced fruit preserves, baking spices, and oak. Just a touch on the hot side, but it takes ice very well.

n: WhistlePig 10 year old Rye, White, and Blue Piggybank, 55%
t: Created to commemorate the 250th anniversary of the U.S. (and priced accordingly), this straight rye comes in
f: Created to commemorate the 250th anniversary of the U.S. (and priced accordingly), this straight rye comes in a piggy bank-shaped bottle that’s hard to ignore. It has a sweet, boozy nose that includes vanilla pudding, maple syrup, toasted coconut, and fudge-covered berries. On the palate, crème brûlée and molasses are augmented by savory mixed nuts and a wisp of mint. It grows more minty with water, which also brings chocolate.

n: Rittenhouse 10 year old Bottled in Bond U.S. 250th Anniversary Commemorative Edition, 50%
t: Rittenhouse’s “barley legal” (51% rye) mashbill is on full display here, lending a thoroughly pleasant sweet
f: Rittenhouse’s “barley legal” (51% rye) mashbill is on full display here, lending a thoroughly pleasant sweet profile from start to finish. The nose has vanilla, Bavarian cream doughnuts, Bing cherries, tangerine, and marzipan. The palate adds powdered sugar and raspberry iced tea, which sits atop a foundation of mellow cinnamon and gingerbread. Those spices take charge on the finish, joined by black and white cookies, fudge, and a tinge of oak.

n: Rare Character Limited Release Straight (Batch 2; 2026), 60.2%
t: A blend of 8 year old Indiana and Kentucky ryes, the nose has attractive dessert-like notes of brown sugar,
f: A blend of 8 year old Indiana and Kentucky ryes, the nose has attractive dessert-like notes of brown sugar, cinnamon-dusted rice pudding, and sour cherry. The palate brings spice into focus with cinnamon and ground nutmeg, strawberry, and cherry cola that creeps in toward the mid-palate and lingers through the long finish. This takes a long while to open up, but its flavors are well worth the wait.

n: Frey Ranch 6 year old Cask Strength, 62.26%
t: This grain-to-glass 100% winter rye is a punchy and potent testament to American craft distilling. The aromas
f: This grain-to-glass 100% winter rye is a punchy and potent testament to American craft distilling. The aromas are layered, with sweet mint, anisette cookies, and vanilla. The palate is fruity and quite sweet, with lemon meringue, candied orange, and honey interleaved with mint chocolate and toasted oak. Water brings out darker fruits, cinnamon, and root beer

n: Dark Arts Whiskey House 8 year old Blunt Blend III Madeira and Armagnac Cask Finished, 56.9%
t: A dual madeira and armagnac cask finish gives this rye an incredibly fragrant nose, where honeysuckle, dark
f: A dual madeira and armagnac cask finish gives this rye an incredibly fragrant nose, where honeysuckle, dark dried fruits, cinnamon spice, toasted nuts, baked apple, and chocolate all mingle. Rich chocolate on the palate swiftly gives way to dark fruit, more baking spice, and espresso bean. The finish is deep and long lasting, with delicious notes of dark chocolate, cooked plums, warming spice, and black coffee.

n: Abraham Bowman Special Release (Release No. 26), 55%
t: This limited-edition aged for 11 years in Warehouse A, one of the distillery’s coolest, fostering slower
f: This limited-edition aged for 11 years in Warehouse A, one of the distillery’s coolest, fostering slower aging. It has a deep, dark color matched by the intensity of its flavor, dominated by the intense deep sweetness of maple, cinnamon apple pie, glazed doughnuts, milk chocolate, caramel sauce, and brown sugar. Spices like clove, cinnamon, and nutmeg make brief appearances before growing mellower and more refined on the finish. It’s lovely, sweet, and tasty.

n: Sweetens Cove Father’s Finish Cuvée Barrel Aged and Toasted Maple Stave Finished Blended (2026 Release), 49%,
t: Jammy and soft on the nose, this limited release from the Peyton Manning and Andy Roddick-backed brand opens
f: Jammy and soft on the nose, this limited release from the Peyton Manning and Andy Roddick-backed brand opens with plums, cocktail cherries, and a hint of bananas Foster. Vanilla and toasted oak provide backbone. The palate is lively, with sharper fruit notes and a more prominent oakiness. There’s more cherry, plus cinnamon, applesauce, and dark choco- late, accenting the fruit forward flavor profile. The finish remains fruity but is well-balanced by toasted oak and coffee beans.

n: Rare Character Limited Release (Batch 2; 2026), 59.97%
t: Some bottles in this batch were accidentally labeled as 2025. This has an alluring nose reminiscent of
f: Some bottles in this batch were accidentally labeled as 2025. This has an alluring nose reminiscent of s’mores, with toasted vanilla, marshmallow, and melted chocolate, plus fudge brownies and cocoa. The aromas continue on the palate, adding chocolate mousse, Nilla wafers, strawberries, and a hint of pipe tobacco. The finish adds Ferrero Rocher, roasted hazelnuts, and a suggestion of cherry. It showcases impressive depth and balance, particularly on the finish.

n: Rare Character Limited Release (Batch 3; 2026), 59.9%,
t: A blend of 6.8–10 year old stocks, the nose is dark and fruity, with strawberry bonbons, raspberry jam,
f: A blend of 6.8–10 year old stocks, the nose is dark and fruity, with strawberry bonbons, raspberry jam, custard, vanilla, and caramel. The silky palate is loaded with chocolate syrup, hazelnut spread, cinnamon sugar, and oak, while earth and leather lurk in the background. The finish introduces raspberry coulis, cherry, and burnt orange, amid toasted marshmallow and warm cinnamon. Well-constructed, with a focused profile that evolves and deepens as you sip.

n: Rare Character Limited Release (Batch 1; 2026), 59.79%
t: Syrupy and rich throughout, this is dessert in a glass. On the nose there’s chocolate chip cookies, fudge
f: Syrupy and rich throughout, this is dessert in a glass. On the nose there’s chocolate chip cookies, fudge brownies, and freshly baked cake with a soft, jammy fruitiness in the background. The palate is sweet but assertive with tart cherry, cinnamon sugar, andchocolate milkshake, plus subdued char and oak. Water brings more chocolate and some light pepper. The finish is heavy and sweet with caramel, baking spices, and sweetened espresso.

n: Old Fitzgerald 10 year old Decanter Series Bottled in Bond (Spring 2026 Release), 50%
t: While younger than some releases in the Old Fitz Decanter Series, this still packs plenty of complexity,
f: While younger than some releases in the Old Fitz Decanter Series, this still packs plenty of complexity, starting with its bready, confectionary nose of brioche, cornbread, and toasted sugar. On the sip, there’s powdered sugar, maple syrup, and fresh-cracked black pepper mixed with vanilla ice cream and berry compote. The finish is gentle, full of sweet vanilla balanced by autumnal spices.

n: Heaven Hill Heritage Collection 22 year old (2026), 64.6%
t: This especially well-aged bourbon uses a heavy corn (78%) mashbill, along with 10% rye and 12% malted barley.
f: This especially well-aged bourbon uses a heavy corn (78%) mashbill, along with 10% rye and 12% malted barley. Cola nut and caramel are the opening acts, complemented by a toasty character on the palate with graham crackers, gingerbread, clove, and barrel spice. The finish is extra long and quite chewy, with a bit of peppercorn spice along with burnt marshmallows, dark chocolate, and a wisp of ultra-sweet banana.

n: Heaven Hill Grain to Glass French Oak Aged Wheated (3rd Edition), 53.9%
t: This series offers elaborate detail as to its mashbill (corn varietal Beck’s 6269) and aging (6 years in
f: This series offers elaborate detail as to its mashbill (corn varietal Beck’s 6269) and aging (6 years in rickhouse W9 on the fourth and fifth floors). The wheat is the star of the nose, which has Nilla Wafers, vanilla cupcakes, and icing. Mocha, caramel-coated peanuts, and Snickers dance on the palate with the first sip. There’s also some candy corn, with a spicy finish that grows ever longer with a little water. Quite tasty.

n: Gambit No. 6 6 year old Wine, Apple Brandy, Sherry, and Tokaji Cask Finished, 48%
t: This is unusual given its finishing in six different casks: chardonnay, cabernet sauvi- gnon, apple brandy,
f: This is unusual given its finishing in six different casks: chardonnay, cabernet sauvi- gnon, apple brandy, muscatel, oloroso sherry, and tokaji. Aromas of baked peach, pecan pie, cherry turnovers, and mixed berries rise up to meet you. The palate is grippy and big to start, with some herbs and tannins. Water brings on quite a change, adding tea, toasted corn, and black peppercorn spice before a somewhat dry finish. An earthy pour.

n: Full Ryde Full Proof (Batch 001-25), 61%
t: Co-founded by NFL Hall of Famer Jared Allen, Full Ryde delivers a bold yet classic bourbon flavor profile.
f: Co-founded by NFL Hall of Famer Jared Allen, Full Ryde delivers a bold yet classic bourbon flavor profile. The punchy nose is caramel-forward, with candy apple and chocolate-covered cherries in support. The palate is more layered, with caramel still prominent, plus coffee ice cream, barrel char, and candied walnuts. Water brings out vanilla, milk chocolate, and dried cherries. The finish is long and surprisingly gentle despite the high proof, with caramel latte and toasted oak.

n: Dark Arts Whiskey House 8 year old Barely Legal (Batch 22), 58.1%
t: From the cutting-edge blending house founded in Lexington, Kentucky in 2023. Named for its mashbill’s “barely
f: From the cutting-edge blending house founded in Lexington, Kentucky in 2023. Named for its mashbill’s “barely legal” corn content of 51%, with the rest comprised of rye and malted barley. It starts out somewhat closed on the nose, and doesn’t reveal much. On the palate, however, sweet orange and vanilla are accented by peppery spice. The finish is nice and long, with excellent flavor integration that really shines through.

n: Frey Ranch 10 year old (Batch 2), 51%
t: On the nose, chocolate orange, cherry cordials, cinnamon, and black pepper mingle. There’s a faint herbaceous
f: On the nose, chocolate orange, cherry cordials, cinnamon, and black pepper mingle. There’s a faint herbaceous quality, too, with whispers of tarragon and mint adding extra depth. The palate is chocolaty and rich, with marzipan, glazed doughnuts, and mixed nuts. Apples, cranberries, and cinnamon emerge with water. The finish is short, but the flavors are excellent: sweet tea, charred oak, and peppery spice.

n: Rare Character Limited Release Straight (Batch 1; 2026), 64.5%
t: A blend of 6–10 year old whiskeys from Kentucky, this offers chocolate, cocktail cherries, cinnamon, vanilla
f: A blend of 6–10 year old whiskeys from Kentucky, this offers chocolate, cocktail cherries, cinnamon, vanilla cupcakes, and baking spice on the nose. The palate moves in a rather surprising direction, adding unexpected nutty flavors of salted peanuts and Nutella alongside dark roast, cocoa, and a bit of rum raisin ice cream. The cocoa stays in-frame for the finish, which also features caramel, cinnamon, nutmeg, and even more dark chocolate.

n: Nc’nean AON Moscatel Single Cask (No. 17–165)
t: Distilled in 2017, this single cask has a heady nose of glacé cherry, ginger root, dried vine fruit,
f: Distilled in 2017, this single cask has a heady nose of glacé cherry, ginger root, dried vine fruit, blueberry muffin, butter toffee, marmalade peel, and festive spices. Orange marmalade on the taste buds, with the spices ramping up to a lengthy peppery buzz, layering on gingerbread and ripe fleshy plum; a splash of water delivers a sweeter profile of sugar-coated plums without altering the thick, mouthcoating finish.

n: 2XO Rapper’s Delight Hip-Hop Blend, 52%
t: A limited release celebrating hip-hop pioneers Sugarhill Gang, this opens with a nose full of dried fruit and
f: A limited release celebrating hip-hop pioneers Sugarhill Gang, this opens with a nose full of dried fruit and nutty sweetness, followed by honey and tart apples. On the palate, it remains fruity, but with a distinctly overripe quality, backed by caramel syrup, orange curaçao, and charred oak. As it evolves in the glass, the oak is dialed up, and it finishes dry on the back palate.

n: E.H. Taylor Cured Oak Bottled in Bond, 50%
t: A coveted release, this was matured in barrels built from white oak staves that were air-dried for 13 months,
f: A coveted release, this was matured in barrels built from white oak staves that were air-dried for 13 months, more than double the standard six-month curing time: That draws out more barrel influence in the glass. On the nose, this means gooey tendrils of caramel syrup, burnt sugar, Rolo, vanilla bean ice cream, and some nuttiness. The palate sees more of the same, along with cherry compote, Heath bar, nutmeg, and nougat. More cherries and vanilla on the finish, as well as lush chocolate.

n: Elijah Craig 21 year old Single Barrel (No. 62), 47%
t: This stately bourbon is unapologetically oaky, proudly showing its age. On the nose, beyond oak, there’s
f: This stately bourbon is unapologetically oaky, proudly showing its age. On the nose, beyond oak, there’s crème brûlée, fruit salad, and overripe banana, giving depth to the woody aroma. The palate is surprisingly fruity, with raspberries, blueberries, and peach cobbler, plus toasted oak and leather in good balance. The finish starts with a generous spoonful of brown sugar and cinnamon before gingersnaps, mocha, and tannic oak linger on the back palate.

n: Joseph Magnus Cigar Blend Armagnac, Sherry, Cognac Finished (Batch 489), 56.08%
t: This blend takes bourbon finished in sherry and cognac casks and pairs it with older bourbon, aged 11 to 18
f: This blend takes bourbon finished in sherry and cognac casks and pairs it with older bourbon, aged 11 to 18 years, that’s finished in armagnac casks. The nose is rife with vanilla, strawberry, cinnamon sugar, and a touch of candied ginger. The palate combines those sweeter notes with earthier flavors of sassafras and peanut brittle. Brown sugar pops up on the finish, joined by the flavors of a PB&J sandwich.

n: Kentucky Peerless 10 year old Henry Kraver Old Reserve, 58.5%
t: The first age-stated bourbon from Peerless is a bold one, chock-full of dark and robust flavors. Aromas of
f: The first age-stated bourbon from Peerless is a bold one, chock-full of dark and robust flavors. Aromas of raisin, vanilla bean, baking spice, orange peel, bread pudding, and caramel syrup emerge from the glass. The velvety palate ramps up the barrel char and adds tobacco, softened by more vanilla and baking spice sweetness. The finish is lengthy and brings the focus back to the barrel—wood spice and char reign supreme

n: Knob Creek 10 year old Blender’s Edition No. 1, 53%
t: With Blender’s Edition, master distiller Freddie Noe wanted a sweeter Knob Creek, and that’s exactly what he
f: With Blender’s Edition, master distiller Freddie Noe wanted a sweeter Knob Creek, and that’s exactly what he got. Aromas of vanilla, cassis, chocolate, cherry, and Raisinets waft from the glass. The palate, still on the sweeter side and ripe with plenty of red fruit, shows darker notes, including chocolate, leather, and wood spice. Maple syrup, barrel char, and a hit of peppery spice come forth on the finish, making for a bourbon with robust flavors that should appeal to non- bourbon drinkers as well.

n: Very Olde St. Nick Immaculata Ancient Cask, 59.1%
t: A chocoholic’s Shangri-La on the nose, with double chocolate brownies, fudge, crushed Oreos, and
f: A chocoholic’s Shangri-La on the nose, with double chocolate brownies, fudge, crushed Oreos, and chocolate-covered pretzels alongside plum, raisin, and black cherries. The palate has applesauce, fresh peaches, ripe pears, strawberry jam, and raspberry, all held up by a rock-solid foundation of butterscotch and oak. The long finish adds grapes, sangria, dried apricot, marmalade, and gingersnaps. Captivating flavors and great integration; a bourbon that seems well-suited for scotch lovers.

n: Yellowstone Recollection Series, 55%
t: Even at its slightly elevated proof, this is easy drinking with enough depth to make it a daily sipper.
f: Even at its slightly elevated proof, this is easy drinking with enough depth to make it a daily sipper. Aromas of honeyed grains, cola, and toffee rise from the glass, backed by peach iced tea and vanilla frosting. The palate is nutty, with peanuts and candied pecans mingling with brown sugar, caramel, and cornbread. With water, fresh peaches and a hint of strawberries emerge. The finish balances coffee bitterness and honey sweetness.

n: New Riff 10 year old High Note Collection, 59.4%
t: The nose offers a bounty of assorted fruits—tangerine, dried orange slices, Granny Smith apples, and
f: The nose offers a bounty of assorted fruits—tangerine, dried orange slices, Granny Smith apples, and melon—with water dredging up sweeter notes of salted caramel, black cherry, and vanilla. The palate includes wintergreen, more green apple and tangerine, and a bit of lemon. It truly comes together on the finish, where these flavors meld with York Peppermint Patties and some chocolate. Interesting interplay between the fruit and mint.

n: Penelope 18 year old Light (2026 Release), 70.1%
t: Penelope has dabbled in light whiskey a handful of times, and this release marks its oldest higher-proof
f: Penelope has dabbled in light whiskey a handful of times, and this release marks its oldest higher-proof iteration yet. The whiskey was distilled in Indiana from a corn-dominant mashbill, then aged in second-fill oak for 18 years. On the nose, this translates to a great interplay of fruit and spice: cherries, Raisinets, strawberry milkshake, and a touch of oak spice. The palate yields slightly deeper flavors of chocolate and caramel, alongside berry fruit and baking spice. The finish combines fruit, spice, vanilla, and chocolate, making for a delightful, almost summery sipper.

n: Thresh & Winnow 10 year old 2015 Vintage Single Cask, 50%
t: Koval Distillery made this from organic rye, exclusively using distillate from the heart cut. It offers
f: Koval Distillery made this from organic rye, exclusively using distillate from the heart cut. It offers oatmeal cookies, breakfast cereal, dried berries, molasses, and brown sugar on the nose. The palate is similarly sweet, with even more molasses and brown sugar, plus baking spice, vanilla, caramel, ripe papaya, rancio, and banana pudding, all lingering on the finish. Well-balanced and deep, truly putting its decade-long maturation on full display.

n: WhistlePig Declaration Double American Oak Aged, 43%
t: Released in celebration of America’s 250th birthday, this is bright and sweet on the nose with vanilla,
f: Released in celebration of America’s 250th birthday, this is bright and sweet on the nose with vanilla, butter cake, and floral honey. The sip introduces cut wood and dried grains, with apple fritters, marzipan, and a hint of earthy cigar leaf. With time, it turns spicy, with cinnamon, allspice, cardamom, and pepper providing contrast to the sweeter flavors. The finish is short but balanced with vanilla and honey tempered by oak and black pepper.

n: Rebel Kyle Busch Single Barrel Select (No. 86213), 54%
t: Picked by recently departed NASCAR legend Kyle Busch, this has notes of ginger ale, key lime pie, vanilla
f: Picked by recently departed NASCAR legend Kyle Busch, this has notes of ginger ale, key lime pie, vanilla frosting, and baked berries. It has an interesting palate of powdered sugar, toffee, shortbread cookies, and burnt sugar. The finish adds caramel, cream soda, and, at the very end, hints of dark chocolate. The palate bites occasionally, but a few drops of water go a long way in taming it.

n: Heaven Hill 13 year old Deatsville Commemorative Edition (Rickhouse AA Floor 3), 54.5%
t: The mashbill (78% corn, 10% rye, and 12% malted barley) is the same recipe used for many of its other
f: The mashbill (78% corn, 10% rye, and 12% malted barley) is the same recipe used for many of its other bourbons, including Elijah Craig and Evan Williams. On the nose, there’s tobacco, clove, baking spice, earthiness, oak, and toasted marshmallow; an intriguing mix. The palate is well spiced and a tad heavy onthe wood, but it’s balanced by a pleasant heaping of vanilla frosting. The finish runs hot, and carries on for quite a while, led by spice.

n: AJ Bond, 47.5%
t: Sazerac’s debut Tennessee whiskey, made at its distillery in La Vergne. Dried herbs, cara- melized sugar,
f: Sazerac’s debut Tennessee whiskey, made at its distillery in La Vergne. Dried herbs, cara- melized sugar, vanilla ice cream, and waffles with maple syrup on an aromatic nose. It’s mouth-coating and smoothly sweet on the palate, with more vanilla ice cream, banana, a zing of lemon, pepper spice, and some new oak. This one offers some wonderful flavors up front, but it’s a bit lacking in depth and still seems a bit young.

n: Virginia Distilling Co. The Split Barrel Project American (Project 1), 45%
t: A 50/50 blend of VDC’s single malt and Green River bourbon. The nose leads with dried apricot, orange peel,
f: A 50/50 blend of VDC’s single malt and Green River bourbon. The nose leads with dried apricot, orange peel, cinnamon applesauce, Triscuits, Frosted Flakes, and French vanilla. Fruits keep coming on the palate, like baked apples, poached pears, and baking spice. The bourbon reveals itself on the finish, adding vanilla custard and oak amid familiar orchard fruits and plum. An interesting blending showcase, but it’d be even better with deeper integration.

n: Dark Arts Whiskey House 9 year old Ripple Rye II Maple Syrup Barrel & Amburana Oak Stave Finished, 54.7%
t: This Indiana-sourced 95% rye, 5% malted barley weaves prickly rye spice and very prominent cinnamon notes
f: This Indiana-sourced 95% rye, 5% malted barley weaves prickly rye spice and very prominent cinnamon notes with maple syrup sweetness, creating a whiskey perfect for a winter’s night dram. On the nose, cinnamon and maple ring loud and clear, with muted mint and sweet herbs providing depth. The sip is maple syrup forward with charred oak, toasted cinnamon, and apple cider. On the finish, the rye spice shines, fading slowly into cinnamon stick and peppercorn.

n: Filmland The Malted Mummy Oak IPA Barrel Aged, 43%
t: This Iowa single malt welcomes you with intriguing aromas of old books in a musty attic, plus hazelnuts,
f: This Iowa single malt welcomes you with intriguing aromas of old books in a musty attic, plus hazelnuts, peanut butter, chocolate sprinkles, and dried berries emerging over time. The palate has Ferrero Rocher, dried cranberries, bruised apples, apricot, and cinnamon powder. The IPA cask shows its hand on the finish, incorporating semi-sweet cocoa with background flavors of malt, nuts, and just a kiss of hops.

n: Michter’s 10 year old Single Barrel Kentucky (2026 Release), 46.4%
t: This well-aged rye is a testament to balance, with dessert sweetness and earthy spice present in nearly equal
f: This well-aged rye is a testament to balance, with dessert sweetness and earthy spice present in nearly equal measure. Aromas of licorice, vanilla, caramel, and clove, plus apple pie round out the nose. The sip is straightforward with cherry cola, peanut butter, and milk chocolate dueling withcloves, gingerbread, and spiced oak. The finish has good length and hints at the whiskey’s age with oak tannins and leather in the foreground.

n: Widow Jane 10 year old Tequila Ocho Tequila Cask Finished Blend of Straights (Blend No. 8), 45.5%
t: This is a follow-up to a Tequila Ocho expression released in 2022 that was aged for 8 weeks in Widow Jane
f: This is a follow-up to a Tequila Ocho expression released in 2022 that was aged for 8 weeks in Widow Jane bourbon barrels. Cherry cheesecake, berry smoothie, custard, nougat, and peanut butter cookies mingle with dried flowers on the nose. The palate has chocolate, baking spice, toffee, and a bit of agave. The finish adds Bing cherry, vanilla cream, oak, and milk chocolate.

n: Penelope Classic Series (2026 Release); 46%
t: An easygoing straight MGP rye with an odd mashbill of 93% rye and 7% malted barley, compared to the more
f: An easygoing straight MGP rye with an odd mashbill of 93% rye and 7% malted barley, compared to the more common 95/5 recipe. The nose is reminiscent of a New York deli, with dill, spicy brown mustard, toasted rye bread, and brown sugar. Prickly spices, in the form of ground black pepper, cumin, coriander, and cinnamon applesauce, appear on the palate. It veers off in a sweeter direction on the finish, with ripe pear, white pepper, and churros.

n: Penelope Classic Series, 46%
t: Penelope’s first-ever Kentucky straight bourbon has a very traditional and rustic profile. On the nose, it
f: Penelope’s first-ever Kentucky straight bourbon has a very traditional and rustic profile. On the nose, it presents black cherry gelato, kettle corn, cinnamon powder, and chocolate, with vanilla cream emerging after adding water. The palate has assorted spices, spiced chocolate, fudge, honey, and more cherry. Chocolate-dipped strawberries emerge on the finish, which retains some of the honey sweetness and spice from the palate.

n: Penelope Cooper Series Riviera Rosé Wine Cask Finished, 47%
t: This blend of light whiskey and bourbon finished in rosé barrels is delicate and nuanced, full of summery
f: This blend of light whiskey and bourbon finished in rosé barrels is delicate and nuanced, full of summery fruit and bright floral flavors. On the nose, there’s berry jam, Granny Smith apples, and sweet potpourri with just a hint of lightly charred oak. The palate brings lemonade, vanilla ice cream, peaches, and pears and is quite soft, in both mouthfeel and boldness. The finish is quiet, too, with a balanced mix of berries and fresh-cut flowers.

n: Woodinville 6 year old, 45%
t: Now carrying a 6 year old age statement, Woodinville’s flagship bourbon has aromas of vanilla extract,
f: Now carrying a 6 year old age statement, Woodinville’s flagship bourbon has aromas of vanilla extract, chocolate-covered cherries, and a rustic woodiness reminiscent of an extin- guished campfire.
