The palate is fruitier, with orange and peaches blending well with black tea and cinnamon candies. The woodiness of the nose is more subdued on the palate, giving the sip backbone and a little bite. The finish is earthier, with charred oak, unsweetened cocoa, and espresso fading slowly.

n: Redwood Empire Pipe Dream Toasted Triple Finish (Batch 001), 46%
t: Finished in a trio of toasted French, Hungarian, and garryana oak barrels. Grape jam, nectarines, Gala
f: Finished in a trio of toasted French, Hungarian, and garryana oak barrels. Grape jam, nectarines, Gala apples, and butterscotch on an uncharacteristically closed nose. The palate includes peanut brittle, Reese’s Pieces, cinnamon sugar, and vanilla. It grows spicier on the finish, adding flavors of cinnamon, nutmeg, and Hershey’s chocolate. The flavors themselves are solid, but they’re generally shy and reticent, never really coming out to play.

n: Penelope Cooper Series Rio Honey and Amburana Double Cask Finished Straight (2026 Release), 49%
t: It’s all amburana on the nose, with warm Cinnabon, Cinnamon Toast Crunch, powdered sugar, cream cheese, and
f: It’s all amburana on the nose, with warm Cinnabon, Cinnamon Toast Crunch, powdered sugar, cream cheese, and caramel. The palate is syrupy, offering heather honey, cinnamon sugar, coffee cake, and Greek yogurt with walnuts—all of which more or less carry over to the finish, which doesn’t add any new discernible flavors. The secondary maturation is quite strong here, lending a cloying texture and overshadowing the base flavors of the bourbon.

n: High West Cask Strength Blend of Straights, 58.5%
t: First introduced in 2023, this expression has been released in occasional limited-edition batches since then.
f: First introduced in 2023, this expression has been released in occasional limited-edition batches since then. Cherries and red berries lead the way on the nose, with a lovely dry fragrance that’s balanced by oak. The palate is sweet and well-spiced, with cherry tart and raspberry coulis, but a bit hot in carrying its proof. Chocolate notes on the finish are accompanied by more cherry and red berry.

n: Michter’s Limited Release US*1 Barrel Strength (Barrel 25B0605; 2025 Release), 54.9%
t: The nose is enticingly fragrant, full of brown sugar, dried orange, barrel char, pipe tobacco, and ripe
f: The nose is enticingly fragrant, full of brown sugar, dried orange, barrel char, pipe tobacco, and ripe cherry. Those cherry notes grow more pronounced and tart on the palate, propped up by black pepper spice, orange peel, raisins, and vanilla, with rye grain underneath it all. The finish ends on a high note—the spice is clear as a bell and the fruit remains top of mind, even as some chocolate and more dessert-like flavors creep in.

n: Old Forester 1924 (2026 Release), $50%
t: A limited annual release celebrating Old Forester receiving its medicinal distilling license during
f: A limited annual release celebrating Old Forester receiving its medicinal distilling license during Prohibition in 1924. Carrying a 10-year age statement, this has a slightly higher corn ratio of 79%, compared to 72% for the traditional recipe. Milk chocolate, cherry, and dried herbs on the nose, with more chocolate and herbs on a warm, expansive, full-bodied palate that’s filled with depth and flavor. Amazingly well balanced; soft but highly flavorful.

n: Blue Hanger 26 year old 14th Edition, 45.6%
t: Drawn from six bourbon hogs- heads and one sherry butt, this has aromas of vanilla, panettone, pecan pie,
f: Drawn from six bourbon hogs- heads and one sherry butt, this has aromas of vanilla, panettone, pecan pie, dark maple syrup, milk chocolate, citrus peel, and cinnamon powder. It’s thick, with a glossy mouthfeel and layers of honeycomb, vanilla, caramel, sour apple candy, brown sugar, dried fruits, and baking spices. Waves of vanilla, cinnamon cookies, dried apple rings, and a hint of espresso on the finish. After more than a decade of no new expressions, this is a triumphant return to glory.

n: Tormore 10 year old Blueprint Cream Sherry Cask, 48%
t: Part of a trio of reworkings of the Tormore core range (hence the name Blueprint) under new owner Elixir
f: Part of a trio of reworkings of the Tormore core range (hence the name Blueprint) under new owner Elixir Distillers, which acquired the distillery from Pernod Ricard in 2022. This decadent single malt spent 10 years in cream sherry casks, and it shows. The nose is rife with vanilla custard, baking spice, cinnamon sugar, molasses, and gingersnaps. There’s spectacular spice on the palate, along with milk chocolate and red fruit. The finish is rich and punchy, and has more fruit and warming chocolate.

n: Old Forester Birthday (2025 Release), 42%
t: Old Forester’s annual release to honor founder George Garvin Brown. Bright and fresh, with soft, generous
f: Old Forester’s annual release to honor founder George Garvin Brown. Bright and fresh, with soft, generous notes of cherry, strawberry, and sweet corn on the nose. The palate offers gooey vanilla, chocolate, and rice pudding, balanced by the oak and accents of peppery spice. A thick texture and similar flavors on the finish, adding tobacco and lively spice. Mellow and easy, but with depth of age and flavor.

n: Angel’s Envy Cask Strength Port Cask Finished (2026 Release), 58.9%
t: This solera-inspired blend has an evocative nose of ground cinnamon, strawberry cheesecake, mellow baking
f: This solera-inspired blend has an evocative nose of ground cinnamon, strawberry cheesecake, mellow baking spices, and more red berries, with water unearthing fruit tarts and saltwater taffy. The palate is similarly sweet and fruity, comprising cherry gelato, vanilla, and Concord grapes, all underscored by nutmeg, barrel spice, and a bit of gingerbread. The finish adds blackberry jam, cloves, spiced cherry preserves, and strawberry drizzle. Though on the stronger side, the port cask flavors are nicely balanced.

n: Ardbeg Dolce, 47.8%
t: Containing Ardbeg matured in marsala dolce casks, there are aromas of ripe apricot, peat smoke, orange
f: Containing Ardbeg matured in marsala dolce casks, there are aromas of ripe apricot, peat smoke, orange blossom, wet wool, iodine, orange fondant, apple pie filling, and a pinch of nutmeg. Creamy and fruity on the palate, with lemon curd, bitter orange, plum, and gentle pepperiness. Turning oily, it reveals papaya, cherry candies, cassia, licorice, and dried herbs, with a thick finish of cacao, sooty oak, nutmeg, and driftwood bonfires.

n: Port Charlotte 18 year old (2026 Release), 52.3%
t: Finished in bourbon and first-fill Rhone Valley red wine casks, this lovely dram draws you in with an
f: Finished in bourbon and first-fill Rhone Valley red wine casks, this lovely dram draws you in with an enticing nose of grilled pineapple, sweet cinnamon, dark red berries, and smoked ham. The palate greets you with waves of briny smoke and seaweed salad over a bed of cooked berries, bright lemon curd, and vanilla wafers. Pineapple reemerges for an explosive finish with kosher salt, black currant, cinna- mon, and oak.

n: Dalmore Select Edition 15 year old (Distilled 2010, Bottled 2025), 49.1%
t: Released in March as a pair alongside a 2007-distilled expression. It was matured mainly in bourbon barrels,
f: Released in March as a pair alongside a 2007-distilled expression. It was matured mainly in bourbon barrels, along with some apostoles and amoroso sherry casks sourced from Gonzalez Byass. Pine, mint tea, earthiness, candle wax, a hint of rancio, and fragrant aged oak on the nose. On the palate, peach tart, baked berries, and light spice. A long finish of chocolate and musty oak. Smoothly textured, beautifully aged, and syrupy but balanced.

n: Kavalan LÁN Single Malt, 43%
t: Named after the orchid, a symbol associated with Taiwan, this was matured in bourbon, port, and STR casks.
f: Named after the orchid, a symbol associated with Taiwan, this was matured in bourbon, port, and STR casks. The nose is beautifully aromatic, with wonderful florals plus cherry gummies, baking spices, dried apple, rose Turkish delight, and baked citrus. Thickly layered flavors of stewed fruits, baked apple, clove, toffee, pomegranate, watermelon syrup, cinnamon, plum, and chile flakes. It concludes with fruity plum flavors and mild spices.

n: Dalmore Select Edition 18 year old (Distilled 2007, Bottled 2025), 46.7%
t: This is part of a duo, released alongside the 2010 version. The nose offers well- aged oak, maple syrup,
f: This is part of a duo, released alongside the 2010 version. The nose offers well- aged oak, maple syrup, chocolate, and old leather. On the palate, vanilla pastries, dark fruit, baked peaches, poached pears, and dark chocolate. The finish is long, warming, and beautifully balanced with rich flavors of chocolate, coffee, licorice, spice, and mellow oak.

n: 15 Stars Artisan Collection 15 and 12 year old Blend of Straights, 54.5%
t: Dark in the glass, syrupy and rich on the nose, this blend of Kentucky and Indiana bourbons comes from the
f: Dark in the glass, syrupy and rich on the nose, this blend of Kentucky and Indiana bourbons comes from the father-and-son team of Rick and Ricky Johnson, who used their popcorn business as the kernel of inspiration to make whiskey. Big notes of caramel and cocoa powder are soon joined by orange marmalade and clover honey on the palate. That sweet bomb is tempered by a spicy snap of licorice and some black peppercorns, with a chewy finish.

n: Milam & Greene Unabridged Volume 3 Cask Strength Blend of Straights, 59%
t: This blend of 49 barrels marries six whiskeys distilled in Kentucky, Tennessee, and Texas. On the nose,
f: This blend of 49 barrels marries six whiskeys distilled in Kentucky, Tennessee, and Texas. On the nose, there’s mint, sage, and toasted almond backed by leather and tobacco leaf. The palate is rich and viscous, with candied pecans underpinned by sweet-and-spicy cinnamon sugar. It holds its proof well, but water draws out sea salt-flecked chocolate and raspberry jam. The finish is long and sweet, with a pronounced cinnamon tingle.

n: Common Ritual Mosaic Chimes Apple Brandy Cask Finished, 50%
t: The apple brandy cask finish on this creates a decidedly fruity experience. Stone fruit dominates the aroma,
f: The apple brandy cask finish on this creates a decidedly fruity experience. Stone fruit dominates the aroma, though there’s plenty of dried pineapple, Juicy Fruit gum, green apple, and key lime pie. The mouthfeel is spectacular, and the palate is packed with peppery spice and cinnamon heat after an initial wave of chocolate, black currant, Raisinets, and blackberries rolls in. A symphony of fruit, chocolate, and spice!

n: Compass Box Hedonism Blended, 46%
t: Red apple peels, white pepper, cherry candy, clove, perfumed florals, nougat, clotted cream, and cream puffs
f: Red apple peels, white pepper, cherry candy, clove, perfumed florals, nougat, clotted cream, and cream puffs rise from the glass, threaded with a firm line of spice. The palate opens rich and creamy, with butterscotch and fruit candies unfolding into lush orchard fruits, caramel, hazelnut meringue, and gentle peppery warmth. Marmalade and apple build depth through the mid-palate before a spritz of orange peel delivers a full, satisfying finish.

n: Midleton Very Rare Vintage 2026, 40%
t: The nose opens with abundant sweetness and fruitiness, as caramel, vanilla, butterscotch, and toasted oak
f: The nose opens with abundant sweetness and fruitiness, as caramel, vanilla, butterscotch, and toasted oak meet sliced kiwi, tangy citrus zest, fragrant grain, apricot, flowers, and fine spices. On the palate, creamy butterscotch, vanilla frosting, and green melon glide into cinnamon powder, ginger root, and mocha. A sumptuous mouth-coating finish of vanilla and gentle spices evokes vintage 2015, delivering a sweeter, creamier experience than others in recent years.

n: Fuji Single Malt, 45%
t: This made its U.S. debut as a permanent offering last October, complementing its single grain and blended
f: This made its U.S. debut as a permanent offering last October, complementing its single grain and blended expressions. The nose offers fragrant bakery notes, vanilla, herbs, and a hint of charred oak. The palate is thick and spicy, with dried orange, char, and a great interplay between oak and vanilla. The long, soft, and delicious finish presents apricot and more orange. Extraordinarily sippable.

n: Bardstown Bourbon Company Discovery Series No. 13 Double Barreled American and Hungarian Oak Finished Blend of Straights, 55.4%
t: An alluring nose pulls you in with scents of spice, strawberries and cream, peanut butter and jelly, and Fig
f: An alluring nose pulls you in with scents of spice, strawberries and cream, peanut butter and jelly, and Fig Newton. It’s a tad hot on the palate, but there’s plenty to enjoy: More succulent berry fruit emerges alongside vanilla bean panna cotta, caramel syrup, baking spice, and coffee creamer. The finish brings caramel flan, concha pastry, crème brûlée, and milk chocolate.

n: Buzzard’s Roost Ambuzzador’s Select Single Barrel (June 2025 Release; Barrel 23-76494), 57.5%
t: An annual release picked by members of the brand’s Ambuzzador fan club. It offers cloves in droves on the
f: An annual release picked by members of the brand’s Ambuzzador fan club. It offers cloves in droves on the nose, along with ginger ale and candied jalapeños. Ground spices like cinnamon, nutmeg, and cumin lead the palate, followed by mustard seed and dark red berries. The explosive finish adds root beer, pickled ginger, vanilla, and brown sugar. It’s certainly a spice bomb, but one that has impressive depth and complexity.

n: Shortcross Distiller’s Duo 5 year old, 46%
t: A single blend combining single pot still and malt whiskeys from Rademon Estate Distillery, matured in new
f: A single blend combining single pot still and malt whiskeys from Rademon Estate Distillery, matured in new American oak and bourbon barrels. Heather honey, malt, oak spices, vanilla sponge, nutmeg, stroopwafel, and tobacco leaf aromas. Sweet and malty with good balance and weight, the opening of honey, brown sugar, and vanilla ice cream is interrupted by a whipcrack of pot still spices, leaving zesty citrus, nougat, apple peels, and waxy honeycomb.

n: Barrell Craft Spirits 18 year old Cabernet Sauvignon & Sauternes Barrel Finished Cask Strength, 62.62%
t: Barrell Craft Spirits takes its wine cask-finishing skills to a new level with this one, its oldest wine
f: Barrell Craft Spirits takes its wine cask-finishing skills to a new level with this one, its oldest wine cask-finished whiskey to date. This blend of Kentucky and Canadian whiskies has a nose of marshmallow, vanilla, herbs, honeyed apricots, and earthiness. A smoothly textured, creamy, and thickly layered palate features peanuts, honey, raspberry jam, and dark chocolate, leading to a long and warming finish.

n: Barrell 7 year old Cask Finish Series Cask Strength Armagnac Finished Blend of Straights, 56.5%
t: A blend of 7–15 year old bourbons from Indiana, Kentucky, and Tennessee finished in armagnac casks. It leads
f: A blend of 7–15 year old bourbons from Indiana, Kentucky, and Tennessee finished in armagnac casks. It leads with vanilla milkshake, Creamsicle, ripe papayas, mangos, honey, and a bit of spice on the nose. The palate has rich cinnamon, raspberry tea, spiced cherry preserves, oak, peanut butter, chocolate chips, and white grapes. The finish adds maraschino cherries, whipped cream, and iced lemon pound cake. A full-bodied bourbon with a pleasant sense of heft and weight throughout.

n: Barrell New Year 2026 Cask Strength Blend of Straights (Bottle 7014)
t: Enticing on the nose; there’s a certain mustiness, as well as dried fruit, caramel candies, pie crust, and
f: Enticing on the nose; there’s a certain mustiness, as well as dried fruit, caramel candies, pie crust, and vanilla custard. Sweet and spice continue to parry on the palate, with vanilla soft serve, Big Red gum, nutmeg, allspice, sugar cookies, and brown sugar coming together. The finish is awash in hot fudge, vanilla, spice—both peppery and baking—and Mexican hot chocolate, making for one delicious journey from tip to tail.

n: Filmland Spirits Moonlight Mayhem! 2 The White Port Wolf, 47%
t: A white port-cask finish imbues this bourbon’s nose with aromas of raisin, overripe fruit, black cherry,
f: A white port-cask finish imbues this bourbon’s nose with aromas of raisin, overripe fruit, black cherry, sweet spearmint, licorice, and a hint of cassis. On the palate, the creamy mouthfeel is punctuated by nice spice and brighter notes of strawberry and cherry sorbet. The interplay of spice and fruit continues on the finish, joined by rich swirls of vanilla and almond paste—a true crowd-pleaser.

n: O.H. Ingram River Aged Flagship (Batch 5), 59.25%
t: Matured entirely on the Mississippi River in a floating rickhouse (actually a converted barge), this is the
f: Matured entirely on the Mississippi River in a floating rickhouse (actually a converted barge), this is the fifth batch of River Aged since its introduction in 2021. Darker in color, with cotton candy and taffy on the nose. The palate offers sweetness and dark berry, with plenty of spice. Overall, the texture is smooth and creamy despite the spice. The finish is long, warm, and thick.

n: Knob Creek Eli Manning’s Bold Pick Cask Strength Single Barrel (2026), 58.2%
t: Knob Creek has collaborated with former NFL star Eli Manning. Herbs, melted caramel, and strawberry shortcake
f: Knob Creek has collaborated with former NFL star Eli Manning. Herbs, melted caramel, and strawberry shortcake are anchored by dry earthiness. The palate is smooth and layered, with coconut flakes, honeyed almonds, chocolate-frosted chocolate cake, and cherry tart, all balanced by jalapeño spice. The finish is long, with balanced sweetness and spice plus layers of lusciously rich flavors, while maintaining great balance despite its proof.

n: The Kaikyo Distillery Hatozaki Omakase Collection Fourth Edition 15 year old Mizunara Cask Finished Straight Malt, 46%
t: The first sip of this deep amber whisky is tart, chewy, and spicy. It opens up on the second sip, revealing
f: The first sip of this deep amber whisky is tart, chewy, and spicy. It opens up on the second sip, revealing some buttercream and layer after layer of wood, but it really sings when a drop of water is added. Then enters a pleasant note of freshly baked pretzels, heavy on the salt, along with light caramel and sweet cookie dough stolen from the mixing bowl before baking.

n: Angel’s Envy 10 year old Cask Strength Caribbean Rum Cask Finished (2026 Release), 55.8%
t: The cask influence is unmistakable on the nose, which offers tropical melons, kiwi, guava, sweet vanilla,
f: The cask influence is unmistakable on the nose, which offers tropical melons, kiwi, guava, sweet vanilla, dill, and black pepper. The palate is spicy and pleasantly prickly, with dill pickles, brown deli mustard, rye toast, allspice, gingersnaps, cinnamon chewing gum, and dried citrus peels. The finish is sweeter, with molasses, cassia bark, and ground black pepper. This is a completely different beast from the flagship, with more depth and much better integration.

n: Two Stacks Triple Sherry Cask Finish, 43%
t: Initially matured in bourbon barrels, then parceled and individually finished in oloroso, amontillado, and PX
f: Initially matured in bourbon barrels, then parceled and individually finished in oloroso, amontillado, and PX sherry casks, this has a gorgeous nose of orange fondant, apple, feisty pot still spices, and blackberry. It’s fat and oily in the mouth, with melted honey, caramelized apple, pepper, clove, toffee, vanilla, pie crust, and black cherry. The finish is long and spicy, with toasted oak. A superb example of what single pot still can offer.

n: Tormore 10 year old Blueprint Bourbon Barrel, 48%,
t: The nose offers honeysuckle, peaches, marshmallow, and pleasant waxiness. Dessert notes of honey and vanilla,
f: The nose offers honeysuckle, peaches, marshmallow, and pleasant waxiness. Dessert notes of honey and vanilla, milk chocolate, and blackberries on the palate. Good length on the finish, with more apricot, vanilla, chocolate, and spice. Nothing complex to contemplate here, just a great whisky.

n: Two Stacks Double Barrel, 43%
t: Distilled and matured at Great Northern Distillery, Two Stacks blends 50% triple distilled oloroso sherry
f: Distilled and matured at Great Northern Distillery, Two Stacks blends 50% triple distilled oloroso sherry cask-matured single malt with 40% double distilled single malt and 10% peated single malt matured in bourbon barrels. Nectarine, smoke, white grape, pear, and lemon curd aromas also carry hints of grassiness, eucalyptus, and Band-Aids. Full-flavored, with mango chunks, mandarin, canned peaches, fruit candies, peppercorn, and porridge oats, with a mouth-coating, juicy finish.

n: Dingle, 46.5%
t: Triple distilled and relaunched at a higher proof, this is matured in a ratio of 47% bourbon, 31% oloroso
f: Triple distilled and relaunched at a higher proof, this is matured in a ratio of 47% bourbon, 31% oloroso sherry, and 22% PX sherry casks. Dried red berries, jam tarts, pomegranate, baking spices, and stracciatella gelato on the nose. Gentle honey-brushed brioche flavors with raspberry jam Linzer torte, cinnamon, nutmeg, malt, vanilla fudge, and a slight nuttiness. It rounds off with a smooth, creamy, malty finish with tingling spices.

n: Maker’s Mark 7 year 2 month old Cask Strength, 56.3%
t: For the first time in its history, Maker’s tacked on an age statement to one of its bourbons, labeling the
f: For the first time in its history, Maker’s tacked on an age statement to one of its bourbons, labeling the core cask strength a 7 year old. The nose is pleasant, punctuated by notes of dried fruit, trail mix, oak spice, vanilla, salted nuts, and caramel. On the palate, many of those aromas are replicated, and they’re joined by yogurt-covered raisins, date cookies, and a little dark chocolate. Rich chocolate carries this one home.

n: Clan Colla 7 year old, 46%
t: Finished in Panamanian rum casks, this sourced whiskey was initially matured in bourbon barrels. A rather
f: Finished in Panamanian rum casks, this sourced whiskey was initially matured in bourbon barrels. A rather attractive nose balances ripe cantaloupe, dried pear, caramel- ized apple, gooseberry, and kiwi, with caramel, vanilla fudge, butterscotch, and marshmallow. Sweet and fruity, with Starburst, banana taffy, stone fruits, grapefruit, baking spice, apple, porridge, and hints of milk chocolate. A chewy finish of dried fruit and vanilla. There’s a lot to like here.

n: Skellig Six 18, 43%
t: Skellig matured, finished, and blended this combination of triple-distilled single pot still whiskeys matured
f: Skellig matured, finished, and blended this combination of triple-distilled single pot still whiskeys matured in bourbon, PX sherry, and peated casks. Clouds of baking spices mingle with aromas of light peat, vanilla, berry fruit coulis, leather, and candy cola bottles. It brings warm spiced fruitcake, cola, clove, and gentle smoke to the palate, before a chewy finish of raisins, black licorice, leather, and black pepper.

n: Redbreast Moscatel Wine Cask Finish, 46%
t: This fifth Iberian Series release was initially matured in American whiskey and Spanish oloroso sherry casks,
f: This fifth Iberian Series release was initially matured in American whiskey and Spanish oloroso sherry casks, then finished 16 months in Málaga moscatel casks from Bodegas Quitapenas. Bramley apple, blueberry compote, nutmeg, damsons, and expressed peel oils fill the nose. An intense blueberry fruiti- ness starts the palate, with honeyed plum, toffee, cracked black pepper, and dried herbs that develop a rich creaminess before a finish of herbs and spicy fruit.

n: Dingle, 46.5%
t: This is intriguing and invites closer inspection, as savory layers of peppercorn, dried herbs, and leather
f: This is intriguing and invites closer inspection, as savory layers of peppercorn, dried herbs, and leather wrap around red apple and blackberry aromas. Tarragon stands out among the herbal notes, and pot still spices mingle with flavors of stewed fruits, dried banana, rowanberry jelly, hazelnut butter, and nutmeg. Matured in a ratio of 59% bourbon barrels, 33% oloroso sherry casks, 4% Pedro Ximénez sherry casks, and 4% red wine casks.

n: Killowen Rum & Raisin, 55%
t: Distilled at Great Northern Distillery, this is initially aged in bourbon barrels before being finished in PX
f: Distilled at Great Northern Distillery, this is initially aged in bourbon barrels before being finished in PX sherry butts and Killowen’s own dark rum casks. The nose has fig, prune, vanilla extract, raisin, toasted coconut, leather, and licorice. It starts out pretty hot, bringing flavors of warm gingerbread, raisins, dates, walnuts, fig roll, fried sweet plantain, and pecans, exiting with menthol, peppermint, caramelized brown sugar, and chewy dates.

n: Middle West 5 year old Double Cask Collection Napoleon Sun-Soaked Calvados Cask Finished, 61.9%
t: After 4 years in new oak, Middle West gives this a year of extra maturation in French apple brandy casks,
f: After 4 years in new oak, Middle West gives this a year of extra maturation in French apple brandy casks, creating an autumnal sip with excellent balance. On the nose, there are apples, figs, and sugar cookies, plus a hint of barrel char to round out the sweet aromas. The sip is robust and oaky, with dark chocolate, apple cider doughnuts, and gingersnaps. The finish is long and toasty, with baked apples and toasted oak.

n: Common Ritual Alter + Bloom Blend, 57%
t: A hefty dose of breadiness floats from the glass, evoking freshly baked cinnamon-raisin bread,
f: A hefty dose of breadiness floats from the glass, evoking freshly baked cinnamon-raisin bread, chocolate-covered pretzels, fudge brownies, cassis, and black raspberry jam. The palate is hot, well-spiced, and packed with more jammy flavors, hints of oak, butterscotch, and sliced pear. Wood is forceful on the finish, but it’s soon softened by dark chocolate, caramel syrup, orange marmalade, and gingersnaps. A delightfully complex and flavorful dram.

n: Stoll & Wolfe Single Barrel (No. 1225), 53.50%
t: This Pennsylvania distillery focuses on reviving historic rye expressions, in this case the state’s famed
f: This Pennsylvania distillery focuses on reviving historic rye expressions, in this case the state’s famed Monongahela style. Chocolate and rye spice on the nose lead to a soft palate that offers stewed red fruits, cinnamon, pepper, and more rye spice. On the finish, baked raspberries and blackberries, vanilla, and just the right amount of spice. Assertive but well balanced and with much to offer.

n: Shortbarrel The Afterswarm Meadowfoam Double Barrel Toasted Honey Cask Finished, 54.3%
t: The nose calls to mind a fall county fair, bringing brown sugar, caramel-dipped apples, freshly baked apple
f: The nose calls to mind a fall county fair, bringing brown sugar, caramel-dipped apples, freshly baked apple pie, cherry, and cinnamon. Spices take the wheel on the palate, offering cinnamon stick, allspice, ground nutmeg, pickled ginger, and hot pepper, all underscored by a pleasant honey-maple sweetness. Chocolate-covered chiles lead the finish, joined by more honey, cinnamon, and very subtle flowers. Despite its nearly year-long finish, it’s very well-balanced throughout.

n: Redwood Empire Haystack Needle, 59.6%
t: The nose of this 8 year old single barrel opens with candied orange, pine, black pepper, and an abundance of
f: The nose of this 8 year old single barrel opens with candied orange, pine, black pepper, and an abundance of baking spice, particularly cinnamon. On the luscious palate, more cinnamon tumbles out, and it’s hot but not painfully so; the heat is balanced by creamy breve coffee, peppery spice, orange peel, a little chocolate, and a lick of lemon frosting. Chocolate coffee cake emerges on the finish, but rich spice remains the ringleader.

n: Bardstown Bourbon Co. Origin Series Bottled in Bond, 50%
t: This 6 year old wheated bourbon leads with maraschino cherry, raisin, cinnamon-swirl ice cream, torched brown
f: This 6 year old wheated bourbon leads with maraschino cherry, raisin, cinnamon-swirl ice cream, torched brown sugar, and vanilla milkshake on the nose. The palate has dark chocolate, barrel spice, cinnamon sugar, caramel, and hints of blackberry. It jolts awake on the finish with more chocolate and vanilla alongside moreish earthy flavors of cigar wrapper, cocoa nibs, leather, and dark berries. An easygoing and well-constructed sipper.

n: Living Soul 15 year old (Batch 2), 46%
t: A solera-aged blend of Glenrothes single malt and North British single grain from independent bottler Whisky
f: A solera-aged blend of Glenrothes single malt and North British single grain from independent bottler Whisky Souls. The pleasant nose offers orange marmalade, custard, marzipan, and lemon curd. Sherry influence from the Glenrothes shines on the palate with wine-soaked fruits, dark chocolate, raspberry-filled Godiva, burnt orange, and a touch of anise. It evolves on the finish with dark chocolate, toasted marshmallows, grape jam, cherry preserves, and a hint of smoke. Excellent harmony of flavors.

n: Tormore 10 year old Blueprint Toasted Barrel, 48%
t: Aged for a decade in toasted barrels, this is softly sweet on the nose, singing with strawberries and cream,
f: Aged for a decade in toasted barrels, this is softly sweet on the nose, singing with strawberries and cream, vanilla, and berry parfait. Medium chocolate follows on the palate, accompanied by ripe berries, Fig Newton, and sweet grain. The finish is a tad richer and darker, dripping with powdered sugar, chocolate, whipped cream, and berry syrup.

n: Skellig Six 18 Small Batch PX Sherry Cask Finish, 40%
t: A blend of sourced single pot still and single grain whiskeys matured, finished, and blended by Skellig. On
f: A blend of sourced single pot still and single grain whiskeys matured, finished, and blended by Skellig. On the nose there’s sliced apple, dried cranberry, baking spice, raspberry jam, granola, and honey sweetness. Well-balanced and tasty, with marmalade, honey, cherry, and active spices, backed by flavors of raisins, dried cherry, brown sugar, and Cherryade, followed by a mouth-coating finish of spiced red apples.

n: Elijah Craig Barrel Proof (Batch A126), 60.2%
t: The latest edition of this rye, which was our 2025 Whisky of the Year, is a study in deliciousness. Aromas of
f: The latest edition of this rye, which was our 2025 Whisky of the Year, is a study in deliciousness. Aromas of cinnamon roll, cloves, toasted marshmallow, and light red berry greet the nose. The palate is rich but, while hot, never overbearingly so; it’s made mouthwatering by custard sweetness, caramelized sugar, all manner of cinnamon pastry, and torched orange peel. More spice follows on the finish, accented by milk chocolate and mocha latte; endlessly enjoyable.

n: Bardstown Bourbon Co. Distillery Reserve Normandie Calvados and Toasted Oak Barrel Finished, 52.1%
t: This blend of 12 and 13 year old Bardstown bourbons was rested for 28 months in calvados barrels from the
f: This blend of 12 and 13 year old Bardstown bourbons was rested for 28 months in calvados barrels from the house of Christian Drouin in Normandie, France. Baking spice, vanilla, and fragrant oak on the nose lead to a palate of juicy raspberry, baked apples, vanilla, and caramel. Crème brûlée on the finish is balanced by spice and oak. $100/375-ml bottle.

n: Wheel Horse Cigar Blend Sherry, Port, & Armagnac Cask Finished (2025 Release), 50.5%
t: Aged 5 years, it has a mellow nose of root beer, peanut butter, Reese’s Pieces, and chocolate-covered
f: Aged 5 years, it has a mellow nose of root beer, peanut butter, Reese’s Pieces, and chocolate-covered berries. The palate is bolder, with a meld of spices like cinnamon, nutmeg, gingerbread, and graham cracker, then sweeter flavors of vanilla, Bing cherries, and strawberry ice cream. The long finish adds salted peanuts, Cracker Jack, cherry gelato, and frosted brownies. It has a pleasant texture and handles its proof fairly well.

n: Two Stacks Double Barrel, 43%
t: Distilled at Great Northern Distillery, this is now aged up to 7 years in bourbon and oloroso sherry casks.
f: Distilled at Great Northern Distillery, this is now aged up to 7 years in bourbon and oloroso sherry casks. Attractive aromas of vanilla, chamomile tea, green herbs, almond paste, citrus peel, and green wood. Pear, dried mango, black pepper, and nutmeg mellow into custard cream, steeped grain, condensed milk, and fruit syrup flavors. Easygoing, with generous sherry fruitiness lingering on the finish.

n: High West Bourye (Batch 25A24), 46%
t: A blend of bourbon and rye aged for a minimum of 10 years. Nosing the glass is akin to standing in line at
f: A blend of bourbon and rye aged for a minimum of 10 years. Nosing the glass is akin to standing in line at the bakery, with aromas of cherry pie, pastry icing, baking spices, powdered sugar, and cardamom. There are more baking spices on the palate, then cherry cola, vanilla, grape juice, and roasted nuts. The spices are pleasantly sharper on the finish, adding cinnamon stick, torched orange, and cardamom pods.

n: Bruichladdich The Laddie Rye, 50%
t: The first-ever rye from Islay in broad release has a mashbill of 55% Islay-grown rye and 45% Islay-grown
f: The first-ever rye from Islay in broad release has a mashbill of 55% Islay-grown rye and 45% Islay-grown barley, and was matured for 7 years. Herbal and fragrant on the nose, leading to a rich, mouth-filling palate with vanilla, blueberry, and figs. The fruit flavors work well with oak, spice, and herbs. The finish reveals perhaps too much oak, but the overall flavor integration is excellent.

n: High West The Prisoner’s Share Red Wine Barrel Finished Blend of Straights, 51%
t: A blend of bourbon and rye finished in wine barrels that previously held The Prisoner red blend from
f: A blend of bourbon and rye finished in wine barrels that previously held The Prisoner red blend from California, as both brands are owned by Constellation Brands. The color is on the darker side, but the nose offers lighter aromas of vanilla frosting and cream puff. The palate is fruity, with luscious jammy flavors of red berries and orange, followed by more of the same on a long finish.

n: Frank August Case Study: 03 Winter Cover, 53.1%
t: On the nose, this offers an excellent balance of sweet and spice, with layers of mint tea, honey, and Granny
f: On the nose, this offers an excellent balance of sweet and spice, with layers of mint tea, honey, and Granny Smith apple supported by brown sugar sweetness and a hint of grape jelly. The sip is sweet but punchy, with salted caramel and maple syrup contrasted by black pepper and a touch of peppermint. The finish turns spicier with cinnamon, peppercorns, and dark-roast coffee, rounding out a well-composed whiskey.

n: Hayashi 24 year old Ryukyu, 43%
t: Distilled in Okinawa from long-grain Indica rice and black koji, it has an aromatic nose of perfumed oak,
f: Distilled in Okinawa from long-grain Indica rice and black koji, it has an aromatic nose of perfumed oak, jasmine, rose petals, tea leaves, caramel, sugar glaze, and lemon sorbet. Citrus takes the wheel on the palate and finish, offering lemon peel, marmalade, and Jaffa cakes amid other flavors of baking spice, incense, florals, and subtle oak. It’s certainly light on its feet, but flavorful nonetheless.

n: GlenAllachie The Sinteis Series III, 57.4%
t: Distilled in 2001, and matured in French virgin oak and oloroso sherry casks, this takes water well. Neat,
f: Distilled in 2001, and matured in French virgin oak and oloroso sherry casks, this takes water well. Neat, however, the nose has melted chocolate, sweet cinnamon powder, pear, espresso, tobacco leaf, and nutmeg. It opens with chocolate, oak char, spices, and orange peel, adding brown sugar, cinnamon stick, coffee bean, and melted chocolate, leaving a lasting spiciness on the finish.

n: Garrison Brothers 6 year old Bottled in Bond, 50%
t: Extremely dark—the color of Coca-Cola—with a rather herbal nose. The taste of charred peanuts and Reese’s
f: Extremely dark—the color of Coca-Cola—with a rather herbal nose. The taste of charred peanuts and Reese’s Peanut Butter Cups joins with clove, sticky toffee, and bread pudding from this bonded whiskey, distilled and aged in Hye, Texas, where the summer weather is hot and dry, and the winters are cold. Water brings out some flinty notes without suppress- ing the strong and persistent peanut flavor. The finish is chewy.

n: Lagavulin Sweet Peat 11 year old Bourbon Cask Aged, 43%
t: Fragrantly sweet on the nose, with peat smoke, sea shells, cigar box, and dried strawberries. Mellow on the
f: Fragrantly sweet on the nose, with peat smoke, sea shells, cigar box, and dried strawberries. Mellow on the palate, syrupy and smooth—peated but not at all a peat bomb— with strawberry jam, dark chocolate, and sugared coffee. The finish has spice and peat to keep the fruit sweetness in balance. Overall, very light and sweet, almost candied at times. A few similarities to other Lagavulin expressions, but a distinct departure.

n: Clan Colla 11 year old, 46%
t: Sourced grain and double-distilled single malt whiskeys matured in bourbon barrels, then finished in oloroso
f: Sourced grain and double-distilled single malt whiskeys matured in bourbon barrels, then finished in oloroso sherry and peated casks. Aromas take time to open up: lemon frosting, allspice, peat smoke, cookie dough, chocolate chip, new leather, raisins steeped in vanilla extract, and dunnage earthiness. Excellent flavor balance with heather honey, glazed fruit, dried apricot, smoke, clove, marmalade, and more allspice, then a finish of cinnamon cookies and cacao.

n: Kentucky Peerless Toasted (Batch 1), 54.7%
t: Building upon the success of its straight rye and toasted barrel bourbon expres- sions, this one is aged in
f: Building upon the success of its straight rye and toasted barrel bourbon expres- sions, this one is aged in No.-3 char barrels before a finish in uncharred toasted oak. Earthy on the nose, with pine needles, grape candy, spicy grain, and a hint of vanilla. The palate is warm, sweet, and well-textured, offering ripe blackberries, vanilla, honey, and a dash of pepper spice. A long, smooth, creamy finish.

n: Dalmore 17 year old Apostoles, Amoroso, and Matusalem Oloroso Sherry Cask Finished, 42%
t: While this isn’t the first Dalmore to bear a 17-year age statement, it is the newest. Appealingly dark, it
f: While this isn’t the first Dalmore to bear a 17-year age statement, it is the newest. Appealingly dark, it has considerable complexity in the glass, from graham cracker to rye bread and even sweet apples. Water brings out gingersnaps along with a dusting of cocoa powder, and it carries a bit of pleasant spice on the finish.

n: Two Stacks The First Cut Signature, 43%
t: Includes whiskeys up to 8 years old: 80% single grain matured in virgin oak and bourbon casks, 10%
f: Includes whiskeys up to 8 years old: 80% single grain matured in virgin oak and bourbon casks, 10% double-distilled single malt and 2% peated malt matured in bourbon barrels, and 8% single pot still matured in oloroso sherry butts. Cereal, light smoke, peach, zested grapefruit, cinnamon stick, and vanilla frosting on the nose. Then orchard fruit, chocolate brownie, clove, and blackberry lead to a sweet grain, cashew, and peppery finish.

n: New Riff Bottled in Bond Balboa (2026 Release), 43%
t: Made from a mashbill of 5% malted rye and 95% Balboa rye (an heirloom varietal), it opens with sumo citrus,
f: Made from a mashbill of 5% malted rye and 95% Balboa rye (an heirloom varietal), it opens with sumo citrus, loads of cinnamon spice, ripe strawberries, and berry smoothie on the nose. The palate is loaded with hot spice, but it’s tempered by the sweetness of strawberry jam, clove, and creamy Marshmallow Fluff. Pepper, dill pickle, earthiness, heaps of baking spices, marshmallow, and a burst of berries make for a heady finish.

n: Loch Lomond Triple Oak, 40%
t: This rebranded expression, formerly known as The Original, has a bounty of malt character on the nose, with
f: This rebranded expression, formerly known as The Original, has a bounty of malt character on the nose, with honey, creamy chocolate, dried apple, and a whiff of bonfire smoke. The palate is refreshing, with orchard fruit, honey, malt, sour apple candies, peach rings, peat smoke, toasted brioche, and malted milk. The finish is full of American oak character, showing creamy vanilla, smoke, and toasted coconut.

n: Shelby Co. Peaky Blinders Irish Whiskey Oak Stave Finished, 45%
t: This homage to the “Peaky Blinders” television series was distilled by Kentucky’s Green River Distillery, but
f: This homage to the “Peaky Blinders” television series was distilled by Kentucky’s Green River Distillery, but gets a European flair courtesy of an Irish whiskey oak stave finish. Red berries, vanilla, clove, cherry Danish, oak spice, and maple syrup greet the nose. On the palate, those notes snowball into yogurt raisins, jelly doughnut, baking spices, and powdered sugar. The finish is fruity, if a tad biting, but vanilla sweetness smooths it all out.

n: Hinterhaus Calaveras Cask Strength Single Barrel Reserve Wine Barrel Finished (Batch 16), 61%
t: Finished in a variety of local wine casks from California’s Calaveras County, this has an interesting nose of
f: Finished in a variety of local wine casks from California’s Calaveras County, this has an interesting nose of fresh peaches, grapes, cut stone, clementines, plums, and honey buns. The palate brings heat with cracked pepper, cinnamon, more peach, and oak, all of which linger for a long finish that also adds flavors of coffee and lime. The wine cask influence is noticeable at times, but it’s well-balanced against the base whiskey.

n: Bulleit Mesquite Smoked Malt, 46.5%
t: The first-ever departure from Bulleit’s signa- ture high-rye bourbon profile, this 6 year old’s mashbill is
f: The first-ever departure from Bulleit’s signa- ture high-rye bourbon profile, this 6 year old’s mashbill is 65% corn, 30% mesquite-smoked barley, and 5% malted barley. Earthiness, grape jelly, sarsaparilla, and light smoke on the nose. Vanilla, red berries, fading smoke, and lemon cake on the palate, with more vanilla on the finish. A well-made whiskey that could have taken more chances; the smoke never really comes out to play.

n: Shortbarrel Four Grain, 46%
t: The mashbill of corn, rye, wheat, and malted barley lends itself to a nose brimming with trail mix, orange
f: The mashbill of corn, rye, wheat, and malted barley lends itself to a nose brimming with trail mix, orange peel, caramel candies, baking spice, and wood polish. Given its proof, it drinks a tad hot, but there are pleasant notes: more baking spice, semi-sweet chocolate, and brown sugar. The finish delivers toasted sugar, vanilla, and cinnamon candies.

n: Common Ritual Spinning Vinyl Double Barrel (Blend No. 2), 60%
t: A blend of ryes from New York’s Taconic Distillery (95% rye, 5% malted barley) and Nobletons Distilling House
f: A blend of ryes from New York’s Taconic Distillery (95% rye, 5% malted barley) and Nobletons Distilling House (90% rye, 10% malted barley) in Missouri. It has a vibrant nose of spiced pear, lemongrass, muddled mint leaves, orange sorbet, Cinnamon Toast Crunch, and caramel sauce. The palate veers toward spicy, with cinnamon, allspice, jalapeños, oak, and pecan pie. The mid-length finish adds dill and just a hint of orchard fruit.

n: Stoll & Wolfe Pennsylvania, 45%
t: Distilled in Lancaster County from a mashbill of 60% rye, 30% corn, and 10% malted barley, this has a mellow
f: Distilled in Lancaster County from a mashbill of 60% rye, 30% corn, and 10% malted barley, this has a mellow and approachable nose of caramel apple, cinnamon, assorted baking spices, candy corn, and mint sprigs. The palate has Mexican hot chocolate, chocolate-covered chiles, toffee, and tart sour cherries. The finish evolves some of those flavors into caramel, stroopwafel, white pepper, and mocha.

n: Chattanooga Barrel Finishing Series Triple Islay Cask Finished Blend of Straights, 55.5%
t: The aroma of salted, roasted nuts invites you to take a sip of this dark amber whiskey, a blend of three
f: The aroma of salted, roasted nuts invites you to take a sip of this dark amber whiskey, a blend of three smoky malts finished in three different Islay casks. It’s smoky and alluring, with flavors of iron, red meat, and oyster shell that segue to a touch of spicy licorice. The finish is long and somewhat sweet, smacking of salted caramel.

n: Traveller No. 40 Full Proof Blended, 60.5%
t: The second whiskey from Buffalo Trace and musician Chris Stapleton is a higher-proof take on the flagship.
f: The second whiskey from Buffalo Trace and musician Chris Stapleton is a higher-proof take on the flagship. Straight from the jump it’s punchier and spicier, awash with orange zest, black pepper, and plenty of cinnamon. The wood influence is pronounced on the palate, though so are baking spices, leather, and pound cake. The finish skews darker, with chocolate ganache, tart cherry, and vanilla coming out on top.

n: Carlyle Master Blender’s Selection 16 year old, 40%
t: A blend of more than 20 components, the nose on this is rich and sweet with apricot marmalade, buttered
f: A blend of more than 20 components, the nose on this is rich and sweet with apricot marmalade, buttered toast, applesauce, green apple skin, and vanilla pudding wafting from the glass. Tons of baking spice, chicory coffee, toasted nuts, and vanilla appear on the palate. The finish takes things in a slightly darker direction, highlighting burnt marshmallow, vanilla extract, cinnamon, and bitter chocolate.

n: Buzzard’s Roost Double Oak, 50%
t: After 4 years in new oak, this is finished in “proprietary casks,” creating a bourbon that carries prominent
f: After 4 years in new oak, this is finished in “proprietary casks,” creating a bourbon that carries prominent oak aromas and flavors without becoming overly woody or tannic. On the nose, there’s French vanilla ice cream, toasted allspice, cinnamon candies, and charred oak. The palate is well-spiced with more cinnamon, Dr Pepper, and campfire embers. The finish is moderately long and honeyed, with a kiss of barrel-char bitterness.

n: Clan Colla Uais The Triple, 43%
t: Pronounced “Oosh,” this sourced blend contains 50% grain, 25% single pot still, and 25% single malt whiskeys.
f: Pronounced “Oosh,” this sourced blend contains 50% grain, 25% single pot still, and 25% single malt whiskeys. The senses are met with grain notes of golden syrup, vanilla, white pepper, sesame crunch bar, parchment paper, and celery tops. Moreish, with honey, short- bread, caramel, glazed nuts, and peppery spices, it’s buffeted by waves of vanilla, banana, and pound cake. The finish is smooth and mouth-coating, delivering creamy vanilla with a wrinkle of spice.

n: Chattanooga Experimental Single Batch Series Single Pot Still Straight Malt (Batch 047), 47.5%
t: A Tennessee twist on Irish single pot still, distilled from malted and unmalted barley and malted oats. It
f: A Tennessee twist on Irish single pot still, distilled from malted and unmalted barley and malted oats. It has a relatively breakfast-like nose featuring honeyed oatmeal, Cinnamon Toast Crunch, and Nesquik chocolate powder. The palate bears familiar flavors of French toast, oatmeal cookies, and rich dark chocolate, which also show up on the finish joined by nutmeg and cumin. Pleasant, but a bit hot for the proof at times.

n: Johnnie Walker Black Cask Bourbon Cask Aged, 43%
t: Arid and earthy on the nose: hay, spiced oak, orange peel, green apple, and dried raspberries. The palate is
f: Arid and earthy on the nose: hay, spiced oak, orange peel, green apple, and dried raspberries. The palate is soft, mellow, and honeyed—though without much depth— with sweet vanilla, baked apples, corn muffins, flavorful grain, milk chocolate, and mocha latte all accented by peppery spice. Lots of chocolate on a light, flavorful finish. A well-built whisky with some excellent flavors, though decidedly on the lighter side.

n: The Whistler Triple Oak, 40%
t: A blend of 50% single grain, 20% single pot still, and 10% single malt matured in bourbon barrels, with 10%
f: A blend of 50% single grain, 20% single pot still, and 10% single malt matured in bourbon barrels, with 10% single pot still and 10% single malt matured in PX and oloroso sherry-seasoned casks. Sweet grain and floral aromas, with Honey Nut Cheerios, vanilla ice cream, toasted peppercorn, and wood shavings. Mild on the palate, with honey, vanilla, Frosted Flakes, orange zest, caramel, dried apple, and clove leading into a spicy finish.

n: Hayashi Koyo Ryukyu, 43%
t: Made on the island of Okinawa and fermented using indigenous yeast, Koyo is elegant and floral on the nose,
f: Made on the island of Okinawa and fermented using indigenous yeast, Koyo is elegant and floral on the nose, with inviting aromas of rose, white tea, and a hint of lychee. The palate is gentle, delivering flavors of soda crackers, toffee, raisins, and dried apricots. The finish is delicate and short, with orange zest, graham cracker, and more dried fruit fading quickly and cleanly. A solid dram, but too restrained.

n: Old Elk Slow Cut Blended Straight, 44%
t: Slow Cut is named for Old Elk’s extended proofing process, which the whiskey makers say preserves delicate
f: Slow Cut is named for Old Elk’s extended proofing process, which the whiskey makers say preserves delicate flavors lost when a whiskey is proofed over the course of days rather than weeks. The nose is inviting and straightforward, with caramel, gooey brownies, and vanilla frosting. On the palate, the whiskey is sweet and gentle, with brown sugar, toffee, and apple pie. The finish is of moderate length with a kick of black pepper and more toffee sweetness.

n: TX Whiskey Experimental Series: Vino de Naranja Blend, 41.7%
t: Texas whiskey aged in barrels that once held Spanish orange wine? Experimental indeed. It’s considerably
f: Texas whiskey aged in barrels that once held Spanish orange wine? Experimental indeed. It’s considerably dark, with a wisp of cherry cough syrup on the nose. That cherry note extends to the flavor, joined by toasted corn and caramel apple. The finish is long and sweet, but not cloying, given its solid back- bone of wood. Water brings out char and a touch of menthol, along with tart notes of licorice. Not the most complex spirit, but one that’s quite pleasant.

n: Proper No. Twelve, 40%
t: This triple distilled blend of single malt and grain whiskeys is not hugely aromatic, but offers green apple,
f: This triple distilled blend of single malt and grain whiskeys is not hugely aromatic, but offers green apple, caramel, vanilla cookies, and caramelized brown sugar. Smooth and tasty, though not overly complex, with flavors of malt, orchard fruits, honey, citrus peel, toffee, and walnut oil, with robust peppery spiciness. It ends with vanilla, gingersnaps, graham crackers, and fizzy sour apple candies.

n: Judson & Moore (Batch No. 8), 47%
t: Distilled in Chicago from 65% applewood- smoked malt and 35% unsmoked malt. The nose has a barnyard-like
f: Distilled in Chicago from 65% applewood- smoked malt and 35% unsmoked malt. The nose has a barnyard-like graininess flanked by sesame seeds, Asian barbecue, and industrial smoke. Smoke dominates the palate, with burnt ends, savory charcoal smoke, brisket, and campfire embers. The smoke lingers on the finish, blanketing layers of peach, mint leaf, oak, and browned apples. This has interesting qualities, but the smoke overpowers and obscures some of the other flavors.

n: Traveller No. 40 Blended, 45%
t: Traveller brings country star Chris Stapleton and distilling luminary Harlen Wheatley of Buffalo Trace
f: Traveller brings country star Chris Stapleton and distilling luminary Harlen Wheatley of Buffalo Trace together to create a whiskey that, in Stapleton’s own words to this magazine, won’t “turn people off.” The nose is fruity and sweet, with apple pie, vanilla ice cream, and oleo-saccharum made with lemon and orange peels. The palate brings a hint of cinnamon bite along with the same sweet fruits before a short finish that’s all vanilla sweetness.

n: Proper No. Twelve Black Reserve, 40%
t: A 4 year old blend of single malt and grain whiskeys matured in heavily-charred bourbon barrels. The nose is
f: A 4 year old blend of single malt and grain whiskeys matured in heavily-charred bourbon barrels. The nose is a curious mix of balsamic vinegar, licorice, Worcestershire sauce, burnt fruitcake, savory herbs, and hints of black currant. Malty on the palate, with heather honey, smoked orange peel, maple syrup, and robust notes of burnt oak and coffee beans. The smoky finish shows clove and bitter oak.

n: Johnnie Walker Blue Label, 40%
t: This epitomizes the rarity, luxury, and craft of scotch whisky blending. It carries a superbly balanced nose
f: This epitomizes the rarity, luxury, and craft of scotch whisky blending. It carries a superbly balanced nose of peat smoke, toffee, cracked black pepper, and coastal seaweed. A sip brings forth smooth caramel, marmalade, vanilla cream, black pepper, candied orange, and hazelnut cookies, ebbing away to leave hot smoky embers, hints of sherry fruit, and dried citrus wheels. This one sets the standard.

n: King of Kentucky 12 year old Small Batch (Batch 1), 52.5%
t: The nose is loaded with beautifully mature aromas—rich gobs of caramel, fragrant tobacco leaf, potpourri,
f: The nose is loaded with beautifully mature aromas—rich gobs of caramel, fragrant tobacco leaf, potpourri, smoky barrel char, and warm dark chocolate. The palate is spicy, with more melted caramel and dark chocolate. The finish brings chocolate, peanuts, spice, a hint of candied orange, vanilla, and pepper spice. Full-bodied, well-balanced, and with plenty of richness and thickness of flavor.

n: King of Kentucky 12 year old Small Batch (Batch 3), 55%
t: Aged oak, baking spice, and tobacco on the nose. The smooth, creamy palate is filled with sweetness but has
f: Aged oak, baking spice, and tobacco on the nose. The smooth, creamy palate is filled with sweetness but has plenty of backbone and bite—pancakes and maple syrup, vanilla cream, and chocolate, with dried herbs, savory spice, and a pleasant earthiness. A long and flavorful finish is filled with chocolate, coffee, and herbs. Great balance, and with somewhat more pronounced flavors than its lower-ABV counterparts.

n: King of Kentucky 12 year old Small Batch (Batch 2), 53.75%
t: Tobacco, vanilla, almond paste, marzipan, and aged oak on the nose. Spicy on the palate, with more tobacco
f: Tobacco, vanilla, almond paste, marzipan, and aged oak on the nose. Spicy on the palate, with more tobacco and aged oak, plus cinnamon, raspberry jam, cherry pie, and candied black cherry slightly outpacing chocolate sweetness. There’s more fruit on the finish, mainly luscious red berries. Overall, it’s quite a bit more fruit-forward than the other two in the trio, but it’s a nicely aged and integrated whiskey.

n: Jack Daniel’s Special Reserve Tanyard Hill Single Barrel, 68.6%
t: This limited-edition rye has a mashbill of 70% rye, 18% corn, and 12% malted barley, and is aged for 10 years
f: This limited-edition rye has a mashbill of 70% rye, 18% corn, and 12% malted barley, and is aged for 10 years at the top of a rickhouse. It’s a riot of flavor, from Bit-O-Honey to crème brûlée and lemon cough drops. Water brings spice, adding some wasabi and ginger along with tons of wood. Amazing flavor and tremendous balance.

n: Johnnie Walker Double Black, 40%
t: Peaty whiskies from Scotland’s west coast and charred barrels are responsible for the intensity of this
f: Peaty whiskies from Scotland’s west coast and charred barrels are responsible for the intensity of this underappreciated Johnnie Walker gem. Deep, velvety layers of sweet peat with beach barbecue smoke, heather, smoked citrus peel, soot, clove, and dried apricot on the nose. The palate offers dried orchard fruit, pepper, vanilla, creamy caramel, zesty orange, and dense peat smoke, leaving a smoky finish of clove, leather, and dried vine fruit.

n: William Heavenhill 19 year old Barrel Proof (12th Edition), 69.1%
t: A complex, alluringly dark limited-edition release that reveals layer after layer of flavor, combining hearty
f: A complex, alluringly dark limited-edition release that reveals layer after layer of flavor, combining hearty hickory wood, honey, apricot jam, and even the sweet, savory notes of panettone. It’s refined and wonderful, with some piney notes that pair with the hickory to balance out the complex sweetness. A sipper that’s hard to put down, and one that drinks better neat than with a little water.

n: Highland Park Cask Strength Heather, 63.6%
t: The sixth iteration of Highland Park’s cask strength expression, first launched in 2020. Perfumed aromatic
f: The sixth iteration of Highland Park’s cask strength expression, first launched in 2020. Perfumed aromatic peat on the nose, along with grape hard candy and barbecued meat fat. Very peaty on the palate—more peated flavors than in previous expressions—with barbecue, raspberry coulis, pepper spice, and cherry pie. Smooth and fruity on the finish as it gives way to red berries and creamy vanilla.

n: Still Austin 6 year old Bottled in Bond Blue Corn (Winter 2025), 50%
t: Made with 26% blue corn in the mashbill. A touch of maple syrup on the nose hints at the parade of sweet
f: Made with 26% blue corn in the mashbill. A touch of maple syrup on the nose hints at the parade of sweet flavors that arrives after a sip. Rich butterscotch combines with tea and hearty wood flavors, and the finish is long and deeply sweet, smacking of butterscotch pudding and a touch of toffee.

n: Midleton Very Rare 200th Anniversary 28 year old, 54.7%
t: This combines all three styles of Midleton pot still, drawing from five casks, including one parcel finished
f: This combines all three styles of Midleton pot still, drawing from five casks, including one parcel finished in mizunara oak for 6 years. Aromas of exotic spices, vanilla fudge, spiced honey, dried pineapple, lemon curd, sandalwood, ginger root, polished wood, and dark chocolate. Combining pot still spices and spicy mizunara oak makes for pretty special whiskey, with gorgeous layers of tropical fruit, honey, shredded ginger, and shiso leaf.

n: Whiskey Del Bac Normandie French Calvados Cask Finished, 48.5%
t: Aged in American oak before getting a calvados cask finish. In a twist from past releases, this edition
f: Aged in American oak before getting a calvados cask finish. In a twist from past releases, this edition incorporates a lightly mesquite-smoked component. The nose opens with peach rings, Granny Smith apple, lemon curd, and Juicy Fruit gum. More fruit follows on the palate, but it’s beautifully accented by vanilla pastry cream, chocolate mousse, hot peppery spice, and just a whiff of smoke. Berry fruit, mouthwatering spice, and caramel carry the finish.

n: Glenmorangie Tale of Spices, 46%
t: The sixth edition in Glenmorangie’s “Tale of” series, following Tale of Cake, Winter, Forest, Tokyo, and Ice
f: The sixth edition in Glenmorangie’s “Tale of” series, following Tale of Cake, Winter, Forest, Tokyo, and Ice Cream. This offers cinnamon, clove, baked apple, and tiramisu sweet- ness on the nose, with lovely warmth and balanced spice. More cinnamon, then baking spice on a soft, balanced palate, with creamy vanilla on the back palate. The finish offers chocolate, more balanced spice, and hints of red berries. Excellent integration of multiple flavors.

n: Barrell Craft Spirits Toasted Dovetail Rum, Port, & Dunn Vineyards Cabernet Barrel Finished, 61.9%
t: Decadent from the first sip, this limited edition delivers bread pudding, honey, and fudge along with a
f: Decadent from the first sip, this limited edition delivers bread pudding, honey, and fudge along with a roasted, salted nut flavor reminiscent of snacks bought from a New York City street cart. Made from a blend of Tennessee and Indiana whiskeys finished in the above casks before additional time in toasted American oak. It builds to a spicy-sweet finish that digs into your palate and refuses to leave.

n: Compass Box Orchard House, 46%
t: Targeting a fresher, fruitier blend, this reformulated recipe includes a higher proportion of Clynelish and
f: Targeting a fresher, fruitier blend, this reformulated recipe includes a higher proportion of Clynelish and replaces Benrinnes with Glen Moray. Now it’s a zinger, with bright, crisp green apple, pear, sliced lemon, shortbread, vanilla cream, and floral notes. Thick and mouth-coating, with sugared apple, zesty citrus, vanilla, Szechuan peppercorns, red apple, cherry lips, Bartlett pear, and Flying Saucer sherbet. It finishes with rose, apple candy, and vanilla custard.

n: Ardbeg 10 year old Cask Strength (2026 Committee Release), 61.7%
t: A whisky so aromatic that peat lovers will likely smell an open bottle within 10 miles. On the nose there are
f: A whisky so aromatic that peat lovers will likely smell an open bottle within 10 miles. On the nose there are kiwi, pine needles, fennel seeds, hot asphalt, lemon lozenges, iodine, peppery herbal notes, and briny aromas. Sweet and smoky with intense spicy heat on the palate, there’s honey, lemon, shortbread, and maltiness, though water yields sweeter citrus flavors, candied lemon, cinnamon, nutmeg, toffee, and molasses, with a finish of butterscotch, menthol, eucalyptus, and salty seaweed. Darn good.

n: Sazerac Rye Full Proof, 62.5%
t: This is proofed down to its barrel entry ABV before being bottled. Candied orange peel, malted milk
f: This is proofed down to its barrel entry ABV before being bottled. Candied orange peel, malted milk chocolate, and sugared caffe latte on this sweet, balanced nose. A spicy palate, hot but tasty, with more chocolate, candied cherry, and jalapeño pepper throughout. Sweet candied raspberry and dry, spicy grain notes on the finish, with more chocolate, oak, and hints of tobacco. Zesty, sweet, and delicious.

n: Johnnie Walker Gold Label Reserve, 40%
t: Built around a core of Clynelish single malt, the nose has Victoria sponge, blossom honey, pear, shortbread,
f: Built around a core of Clynelish single malt, the nose has Victoria sponge, blossom honey, pear, shortbread, cantaloupe, and banana chips. Creamy and sweet on the palate, it bursts with fresh tropical fruits, honey, panna cotta, vanilla, creamed banana, dried pineapple, and papaya flavors, with hints of passion fruit and citrus. Smoked orange peel stands out in the zesty, fruity finish.

n: Redbreast 15 year old, 40%
t: Matured in bourbon and oloroso sherry casks, the nose is complex with chocolate brownie, toasted oak,
f: Matured in bourbon and oloroso sherry casks, the nose is complex with chocolate brownie, toasted oak, well-integrated pot still spices, blackberry, toasted hazelnuts, prune, and raisin. It’s nutty and oily on the palate; just what you expect from a single pot still whiskey, as the spiciness builds to an epic peak, supported by fig, date, and jellied fruit. Wood spice, oakiness, and clove to finish.

n: Jack Daniel’s Distillery Series Barrel Proof Table Syrup Barrel Finished (Winter 2025, Selection No. 16), 55.7%
t: A 3-year finish in barrels that previously held table syrup—made from corn syrup, cane syrup, cane molasses,
f: A 3-year finish in barrels that previously held table syrup—made from corn syrup, cane syrup, cane molasses, and honey—sounds sickeningly sweet, but there’s a lot to love. The nose is jammy, with cooked cherries, orange peel, cinnamon, almond paste, and spiced rum cake. Black tea and anise on the palate, with cinnamon stick, simple syrup, and toasted nuts taking the spotlight. A very sweet finish—waffles and maple syrup—that’s mingled with spice.

n: Booker’s Phantom Pipes Batch (Batch No. 4), 63.2%
t: Named for Booker Noe’s eccentric hobby of tinkering with pipes at the Beam Distillery in Boston, Kentucky.
f: Named for Booker Noe’s eccentric hobby of tinkering with pipes at the Beam Distillery in Boston, Kentucky. Fragrant and buttery on a warm and inviting nose—fresh cornmeal, French toast, raspberry jam, fiery spice, and oak. The palate is also sweet, buttery, and flavorful, bursting with baked berries, vanilla, ample spice, and drying oats. Plenty of heat, but pronounced flavors. The finish is long and sweet, with the palate’s flavors returning.

n: Royal Salute Kingdom 26 year old Colheita Port Finish, 50%
t: The final edition in the Kingdom Collection trilogy is the brand’s first port cask finish. Aromas of mature
f: The final edition in the Kingdom Collection trilogy is the brand’s first port cask finish. Aromas of mature tawny port abound, with glacé cherry, Red Vines, rich toffee, fruitcake, smoky oak, clove, leather, and dried fig. On the palate, cherry jam, damson, and dark chocolate dance with vibrant spices, plus plum, more spice, and charred oak on the back end, with a dark finish of cacao and blackened oak.

n: Old Potrero California Cellar Series No. 04 Almanac Beer Finished, 57.5%
t: This aged 6 years and 6 months in new charred oak before an 8-month finish in Old Potrero barrels that once
f: This aged 6 years and 6 months in new charred oak before an 8-month finish in Old Potrero barrels that once aged Almanac Beer Co. imperial stout. Classic (and fantastic!) rye notes on the nose: there’s cinnamon spice and pickle juice, alongside rye bread. The palate is richly textured, hot, spicy, and crackling with black pepper, then char, vanilla, and chocolate doughnuts. On the finish, light rye spice lingers, with sweet cream and chocolate milk.

n: Annandale Distillery Storyman, 46%
t: A blend from this Lowlands single cask scotch whisky maker, selected in collaboration with Scottish actor
f: A blend from this Lowlands single cask scotch whisky maker, selected in collaboration with Scottish actor James Cosmo. Pleasant notes of char and a whiff of peat on the nose meld with hints of sweet vanilla. Charcoal and vanilla, pepper spice, and toast on the flavorful, full-bodied, and well-structured palate. The finish is long and smooth, with more vanilla and citrus as the flavors carry on. Well made, flavorful, and balanced.

n: Malloy Hall, 43%
t: Crafted from a mashbill of 74% rye, 11% corn, and 15% malted barley, this is easy to sip at this proof.
f: Crafted from a mashbill of 74% rye, 11% corn, and 15% malted barley, this is easy to sip at this proof. Caramel, peppery spices, heather honey, Biscoff, baked rosemary sprigs, toasted marshmallow, and muscovado sugar on the nose. The citrusy palate reflects the sweetness, spice, and herbal notes of the aromas. Toasted rye, pepper, and gingersnap deliver a satisfying spicy finish.

n: Nc’nean Quiet Rebels Simon, 48.5%
t: Each Quiet Rebels release is chosen by a Nc’nean team member. This one was selected by distiller and beer
f: Each Quiet Rebels release is chosen by a Nc’nean team member. This one was selected by distiller and beer fanatic Simon Hewitt. It was finished in Innis & Gunn stout casks after an initial maturation in shave-toast-rechar (STR) casks. The nose is enticing, with juicy dark fruits enveloped in coffee and chocolate; think an Americano with a chocolate chip cookie and black cherry muffin. The palate is bold, intense, and moreish, with milk choco- late, black coffee, black pepper, chocolate ganache, and cinnamon stick.

n: MilHòc Première Flamme Single Grain, 50%
t: Distilled from a mash of 54% corn and 46% French malted barley, this grain whisky ages 4-5 years in toasted
f: Distilled from a mash of 54% corn and 46% French malted barley, this grain whisky ages 4-5 years in toasted American oak, bourbon barrels, and armagnac casks. On the nose, there’s baked apples, white grape juice, and cherry cola, with a whisper of dark rye bread. The fruits are more muted on the palate, where raisins, chocolate-dipped strawberries, and funnel cake take the lead. The finish is long, with fruit tart and chocolate-covered espresso beans.

n: Aberfeldy 12 year old (2025 Release), 40%
t: Matured in a combination of bourbon and sherry casks, this is a distinctive introduction to Aberfeldy’s
f: Matured in a combination of bourbon and sherry casks, this is a distinctive introduction to Aberfeldy’s signature Highland flavors. Golden syrup cake, plump raisins, and brown sugar, with hints of cherry and maple syrup on the nose. Syrupy and rich on the tongue, with gingerbread cake, heather honey, vanilla, baked orange, raisin, candied lemon, ground cherry, and a little singed oak. Caramelized ginger, smoke, and fudge round out the finish.

n: Paul John Christmas Cream Cask (2025 Edition), 48%
t: The olfactory senses appreciate the 2-year finish in cream sherry casks, which brings dried red berries,
f: The olfactory senses appreciate the 2-year finish in cream sherry casks, which brings dried red berries, plum, black pepper, orange zest, and dried stone fruits. This 8 th Christmas edition is expressive and satisfying, with good weight on the tongue, showing active spices, honey, and citrus, then walnut, cinder toffee, raisin, and apple pie, and a finish that ebbs and flows between butterscotch sauce, candied apple, and toffee.

n: Redbreast 12 year old, 40%
t: Triple distilled at Midleton, this classic single pot still whiskey is aged in bourbon and sherry casks. The
f: Triple distilled at Midleton, this classic single pot still whiskey is aged in bourbon and sherry casks. The aromas of pot still spice come to the fore, supported by Red Vines, sherry notes, and baking spices, with hints of pomegranate and tobacco. Silky-smooth mouthfeel with generous oloroso sherry cask influence, showing red apple, raisin, gingerbread, dried cherry, cassis, and a creamy finish with lingering pot still spices.

n: Three Chord Un-Edited Cask Strength Blend of Straights, 59%
t: A blend of 4 year old Tennessee bourbon, 6 year old Indiana bourbon, and 7 year old Kentucky bourbon, this
f: A blend of 4 year old Tennessee bourbon, 6 year old Indiana bourbon, and 7 year old Kentucky bourbon, this starts strong with grape jelly, cherry cola, baking spice, and raspberry rugelach wafting from the glass. For its proof, the mouthfeel is velvety smooth, but soon enough there’s plenty of heat in the form of Red Hots and Mexican hot chocolate. As the heat subsides, sweeter flavors of crème patisserie and baking spice stick out. The experience ends on a delightful note, as rich chocolate and raspberry coulis swirl about.

n: Still Austin Tanager Cigar Blend, 54%
t: Created by master blender par excellence Nancy Fraley, who employed the French “petits eaux” dilution method
f: Created by master blender par excellence Nancy Fraley, who employed the French “petits eaux” dilution method used in cognac making. The nose is resplendent with cigar ash and tobacco leaf, dried strawberries, vanilla, and mellow herbs. The palate features cherry, anise, red berries, vanilla cream, more tobacco leaf, and pepper spice, with a finish of similar flavors. Not super dynamic, but a very worthy accompaniment to a good cigar.

n: Still Austin 7 year old Bottled In Bond (Fall 2025), 50%
t: Texas-based Still Austin’s oldest whiskey to date. An aromatic nose of mellow oak, with wafting herbal aromas
f: Texas-based Still Austin’s oldest whiskey to date. An aromatic nose of mellow oak, with wafting herbal aromas leading to a smooth, fruit-laden palate abounding in red berry, cherry, sweet vanilla, and pepper spice. The finish is long and smooth, with well-integrated flavors of chocolate, raspberry, more vanilla, and spice. The dangers of over-oaking in the Texas heat have been deftly conquered, leaving a fun, flavorful interplay of savory and sweet.

n: Old Fitzgerald Decanter Series Bottled in Bond 11 year old, 50%
t: Dried herbs, oak, and warehouse earthiness on the nose, along with cinnamon, cocoa powder, and a hint of red
f: Dried herbs, oak, and warehouse earthiness on the nose, along with cinnamon, cocoa powder, and a hint of red berries, all gracefully bal- anced and inviting. The palate is smooth and flavorful, with freshly shelled peanuts, dark chocolate, jalapeño spice, with jammy berry notes beneath. Very good length on a light, smooth, and delicious finish that offers vanilla, almond, spice, and honey.

n: Stranahan’s Diamond Peak Local Brewer’s Cask Finished, 45%
t: Stranahan’s annual cask finished release, this one using casks from four local brewers. The nose offers
f: Stranahan’s annual cask finished release, this one using casks from four local brewers. The nose offers lemon, soft grain, new leather, and earthiness. The palate is light, smooth, soft, and creamy, with vanilla, sweet coconut, and peach. A nicely layered thickness of flavors carries on to the finish, which offers rich notes of chocolate, seven-layer cake, light spice, and poached pears. Complex, with a smooth texture and soft mouthfeel.

n: Brother Justus Founder’s Reserve (2025 Release), 62.5%
t: Distilled in Minnesota from pale ale malted barley and aged in new local oak, it has an interesting nose of
f: Distilled in Minnesota from pale ale malted barley and aged in new local oak, it has an interesting nose of vanilla, marzipan, almond paste, hazelnuts, and bruised fruit. The palate is hot and intense, with baked pears, Golden Delicious apples, dates, chai spice, nutmeg, and autumn leaves. More pear, applesauce, and spice carry through the finish, ending on a high note.

n: Johnnie Walker Black Label 12 year old, 40%
t: Built around key malts from Cardhu, Caol Ila, Clynelish, and Glenkinchie, the nose is beautifully balanced
f: Built around key malts from Cardhu, Caol Ila, Clynelish, and Glenkinchie, the nose is beautifully balanced with peat smoke, caramel, dried fruits, generous spices, toasted oak, and hints of dark chocolate. Smooth on the palate, it shows caramelized sugar, toffee apple, peppery spices, and peat smoke, then melted caramel and vanilla essence, easing into a lengthy finish of toffee, smoke, and lingering pepperiness. Classic for a reason.

n: Johnnie Walker 18 year old, 40%
t: Key flavors originate from a recipe that includes spicy Blair Athol, fruity Glen Elgin, and creamy Cardhu.
f: Key flavors originate from a recipe that includes spicy Blair Athol, fruity Glen Elgin, and creamy Cardhu. The nose revolves around apple pie filling, honey, sponge candy, malted milk, gentle spices, and Florentines, with a gentle coastal smokiness. Orange peel oils, dried apple, vanilla, fragrant spices, marzipan, and toasted almond flakes on the palate, with a finish of Chantilly cream, vanilla, and poached pear.

n: Glengoyne 18 year old (2025 Release), 43%
t: Famously unpeated, Glengoyne has been distilled in the Highlands for nearly 200 years, but is aged in the
f: Famously unpeated, Glengoyne has been distilled in the Highlands for nearly 200 years, but is aged in the Lowlands. This expression lures you in with a gentle aroma of toasted bread. Almond and nougat come alive on the palate, along with a faint hint of sauternes wine on the finish. A drop of water brings out some previously hidden earthiness and lengthens the finish. Elegant and balanced.

n: Malloy Hall Sherry Cask Edition, 43%
t: This one was made from Rosalina, Sebastian, and Barke barley varieties and matured in Pedro Ximénez sherry
f: This one was made from Rosalina, Sebastian, and Barke barley varieties and matured in Pedro Ximénez sherry casks. Raisins, baked plum, marmalade, and polished leather aromas, with hints of peppercorn and cocoa powder on cappuccino foam. More marmalade, along with lime peel, black pepper, blackberry, leather, and hints of grapefruit on the palate. The spices subside on the finish with Red Vines and dried vine fruits.

n: Smokehead 15 year old, 43%
t: Briny and leathery on the nose, this single malt from Ian Macleod Distillers starts oceanic and austere
f: Briny and leathery on the nose, this single malt from Ian Macleod Distillers starts oceanic and austere before giving way to a more balanced, sweeter sip. While the nose leans into the whisky’s Islay roots, the palate balances peat, iodine, and salt air with lush sweets like caramel candies, flan, and fruit tart. With a dash of water, lemon zest and tart apples are revealed. The finish is light and harmonious with peat and vanilla.

n: Sagamore High Rye, 59%
t: Calling this release a tribute to Kentucky bourbon and Maryland rye, Sagamore’s 6 year old bourbon is made
f: Calling this release a tribute to Kentucky bourbon and Maryland rye, Sagamore’s 6 year old bourbon is made from a mash of 60% corn, 25% rye, and 15% malted rye. On the nose, it’s densely sweet and spicy, with molasses, brown sugar, caramel syrup, and nutmeg. The palate is well spiced with savory herbs, black licorice, and a pronounced pepperiness. The finish is long and balanced, with vanilla and caramel offset by pepper and char.

n: Three Chord Hard Pressed Bottled in Bond, 50%
t: A 4 year old from Tennessee with a mashbill of 80% corn, 10% rye, and 10% malted barley kicks off with a nose
f: A 4 year old from Tennessee with a mashbill of 80% corn, 10% rye, and 10% malted barley kicks off with a nose reminiscent of a holiday party—pine cones, Christmas spice, and ground cinnamon—plus vanilla wafers and black-and-white cookies; over time, cherries and pear slices emerge. The palate is a tad hot for the proof, but it has solid flavors of vanilla, double-chocolate chip cookies, caramel apple, and baking spices. The finish ties everything in a bow with cinnamon applesauce, oak, caramel, and raspberry coulis.

n: Hard Truth Barrel Finish Reserve Mizunara Oak Finished, 62.3%
t: This straight rye (94% rye, 6% malted barley) is exceptionally dark in the glass, with a cherry cola nose.
f: This straight rye (94% rye, 6% malted barley) is exceptionally dark in the glass, with a cherry cola nose. Cherries abound, hinting at maraschino liqueur, and the copious sweetness is buttressed by a touch of menthol. Water brings out even more flavor, and the finish is delightfully long. Limited release, with 21 barrels made.

n: New Riff 6 year old Sherry Finished Barrel Proof, 55.95%
t: A rare cask-finished whiskey in the New Riff portfolio, this 100% malted rye is brooding on the nose, with
f: A rare cask-finished whiskey in the New Riff portfolio, this 100% malted rye is brooding on the nose, with restrained dark fruit, a hint of sherry cask funk, and a whisper of peppery spice. The palate is more welcoming, with raisins, dried cranberries, and cooked apple backed by mint tea, overripe berries, and muted baking spices. The finish is long, with roasted grain, dried spices, and pepper.

n: Pursuit United Triple Mash Barrel Proof Blend of Straights, 60.9%
t: Two ryes from Sagamore Spirit and one from Bardstown Bourbon Co. make up this blend. It leads with an
f: Two ryes from Sagamore Spirit and one from Bardstown Bourbon Co. make up this blend. It leads with an herbaceous nose of mint and fennel, plus spiced oranges and lemons in the background.
