The sip is citrus-driven, with lemon zest and chocolate orange. With water, it rounds out and shows cinnamon rolls, mint tea, and flan. The finish has moderate length and closes with more lemon and cinnamon.

n: Malloy Hall, 43%
t: Produced at The Distillery in Lambertville, New Jersey from a mashbill of 74% corn, 8% rye, and 18% malted
f: Produced at The Distillery in Lambertville, New Jersey from a mashbill of 74% corn, 8% rye, and 18% malted barley. The nose is inviting with sweet honey, madeleines, ground almonds, and soft butter mints. Granola, toasted nuts, Cheerios, and heather honey on the palate, it’s slightly mouth-drawing until the creaminess breaks through. Then vanilla, marzipan, and cornbread shine, rounding off a breakfast cereal and honey finish.

n: Heaven Hill Distillery 90th Anniversary 9 year old, 53.5%
t: Honoring the distillery’s nine decades of whiskey making. The nose is sweet, offering vanilla ice cream with
f: Honoring the distillery’s nine decades of whiskey making. The nose is sweet, offering vanilla ice cream with vanilla-frosted birthday cake, and coconut. A viscous mouthfeel and a fairly spicy palate, but with luscious notes of chocolate. A long finish offers more chocolate and flavorful undertones of raspberry jam, enhanced by baking spices and wood spice. A bit too spicy at times, but a solid expression.

n: Three Chord RIOT Double Bonded Bottled in Bond Blend, 50%
t: A blend of two bonded ryes from MGP and Bardstown, aged from 4–7 years. It’s fairly sweet on the nose, with
f: A blend of two bonded ryes from MGP and Bardstown, aged from 4–7 years. It’s fairly sweet on the nose, with cinnamon sugar, Cinnabon rolls, coffee cake, and brownies. Spiced chocolate, ground cinnamon, powdered sugar doughnuts, nutmeg, and other baking spices form a well-structured palate with a pleasant oily texture. Those spices return on the finish, a bit sharper than before, now joined by vanilla.

n: Templeton Rye The Hidden Stash Collection 13 year old (No. 1), 54%
t: This MGP-sourced 95% rye, 5% malted barley rye is a strong example of a familiar mashbill and distillery. The
f: This MGP-sourced 95% rye, 5% malted barley rye is a strong example of a familiar mashbill and distillery. The nose is bright and peppery, with heaping dashes of white and black pepper atop a core of anise and vanilla. On the palate, the whiskey delivers a similarly peppery experience, but with added depth from rich caramel and savory herbs. The finish is long and peppery.

n: Three Chord Flipside Triple Wood Toasted French Oak and American Oak Barrel Finished, 45%
t: Toffee and candied walnuts blend with vanilla ice cream and chocolate syrup on the nose, creating a welcoming
f: Toffee and candied walnuts blend with vanilla ice cream and chocolate syrup on the nose, creating a welcoming if relatively simple first impression. The palate shows greater depth with chocolate cake, cardamom, nutmeg, cloves, and a warming spiciness. On the back palate, there’s a rich pepperiness that adds a twist of complexity to an otherwise straight forward pour. The pepper remains on the lengthy finish, mingling with milk chocolate, lightly toasted oak, and sweetened coffee.

n: Three Chord Strange Collab Finished in Pinot Noir Barrels, 49.5%
t: From musician-turned-whiskey maker Neil Giraldo, a blend of bourbons aged 3-6 years and finished in pinot
f: From musician-turned-whiskey maker Neil Giraldo, a blend of bourbons aged 3-6 years and finished in pinot noir barrels from California’s Strange Family Vineyards. Sweet corn, marshmallow, and vanilla frosting on the nose, with lively rye spice. Very sweet yet also spicy on the palate, with the peppery spice accenting a base of vanilla sweetness. The long finishoffers similar flavors. Lively and enjoyable—not just sweet, but also balanced and full of depth and complexity.

n: High Wire Distilling Co. 7 year old Jimmy Red Limited Edition Wheated (Batch 6), 53.5%
t: This release includes wheat alongside the typical Jimmy Red corn in the mashbill. It takes a few minutes to
f: This release includes wheat alongside the typical Jimmy Red corn in the mashbill. It takes a few minutes to open up, but it rewards your patience with a lovely nose of cherry gelato, caramel hard candies, brown sugar, chocolate-covered berries, and peanut butter. The palate is chewy and well-textured, with salted peanuts, barrel spice, pepper, vanilla, oak, and lush black cherries that linger through the finish.

n: Malloy Hall, 43%
t: Matured in a combination of bourbon and sherry casks, this was distilled from Rosalina, Sebastian, and Tipple
f: Matured in a combination of bourbon and sherry casks, this was distilled from Rosalina, Sebastian, and Tipple malted barley varieties. Lemon curd, vanilla, golden syrup, white pepper, and lime aromas, with floral top notes and a pleasant grassiness. Honeyed, silken, and beautifully weighted with lemon meringue pie, sweet peanut candy, green apple, vanilla cookie, and candied lemon flavors. The finish is spicy, with graham cracker and vanilla frosting.

n: Woodford Reserve Master’s Collection Sweet Oak (Series No. 21), 55.2%
t: The 21st release in Woodford’s high-end Master’s Collection aged entirely in chinkapin oak barrels. Native to
f: The 21st release in Woodford’s high-end Master’s Collection aged entirely in chinkapin oak barrels. Native to eastern and central parts of North America, chinkapin tends to lend sweeter notes to a whiskey, and that’s well illustrated here—the nose is rife with ripe cherries, brown sugar-cinnamon butter, and a bright hint of lemon peel. There’s a chewiness to the palate, with more cherry fruit, a crack of black pepper, oak spice, and vanilla soft serve. Cherry reappears on the dry finish, joined by semi-sweet chocolate, peppery spice, and sweet vanilla.

n: Garrison Brothers Guadalupe Port Cask Finished (2025 Release), 53.5%
t: The influence of a port cask muscles its way right to the front. The nose kicks off with Whoppers,
f: The influence of a port cask muscles its way right to the front. The nose kicks off with Whoppers, pomegranate seeds, and vanilla, with barrel char and ash playing supporting roles. Even more char on the palate, where there’s a meaty, gamey quality, but it’s tempered by jammy raspberry and hot spice. Ultra-ripe berries, spice, Black Forest cake, vanilla pudding, and a lick of anise make for a flavorful finish.

n: Whistlepig The Boss Hog XII Feather & Flame New American Oak & Pulque Curado de Cacao Barrel Finished (Barrel No. 10), 52.4%
t: Finished in barrels that previously held pulque curado de cacao—a chocolate-flavored beverage made from
f: Finished in barrels that previously held pulque curado de cacao—a chocolate-flavored beverage made from fermented agave sap—infused with three types of Mexican peppers: chiltepín, guajillo, and pasilla. Citrus, lemon icing, vanilla, lemongrass, and Linzertorte create a zesty and fresh nose. The palate has dill, Red Hots, cherry cola, strawberry jam, pomegranate, and honey. The secondary cask really shines on the explosive finish, which has ghost pepper rub, Mexican hot chocolate, gingery Thai spice, vanilla, and oak.

n: Lochlea Single Estate Our Barley, 46%
t: Matured in a combination of bourbon, sherry, and STR casks, the nose is enticing and approachable with fresh
f: Matured in a combination of bourbon, sherry, and STR casks, the nose is enticing and approachable with fresh pear, lime marmalade, jellied fruits, and dried orange slices. The palate opens with canned pears, pepper, and clove, adding a distinctive macadamia nuttiness, then marmalade, followed by spiced grapefruit and a waxy finish with bright citrus and warming clove.

n: Ampersand Opimus 15 year old Tokaji Wine Cask Finished, 58.3%
t: Sugar cookies, raspberries, fig cookies, and cola rise from the glass with a hint of overripe banana and
f: Sugar cookies, raspberries, fig cookies, and cola rise from the glass with a hint of overripe banana and varnished oak in the background. With time, bitter fruit and oak come through on the palate, led by grapefruit, fresh cranberries, and toasted maplewood. The palate is similarly jam-packed, vacillating from sweet cherry pie to citrus pith, over-steeped tea, and barrel char. The finish is of moderate length and quite tannic and oaky. Tasty, but perhaps could be a bit more cohesive.

n: Carlyle 12 year old Master Blender’s Selection, 40%
t: Comprising 20 whiskies aged in bourbon barrels, this opens with a sweet and citrusy nose of caramel, vanilla
f: Comprising 20 whiskies aged in bourbon barrels, this opens with a sweet and citrusy nose of caramel, vanilla wafers, lemon meringue, lime zest, burnt orange, and marzi- pan. It has a fairly light-bodied yet flavorful palate, with baked peach, apricot slices, lemon tart, orange sorbet, and gently spiced orchard fruits. The fruits carry over to the finish, joined by malt and chocolate chips.

n: Milam & Greene Provisions Blend of Straights (1st Edition), 40%
t: This blend of pot distilled Texas and Kentucky bourbons opens with a vanilla and toffee-heavy nose that’s
f: This blend of pot distilled Texas and Kentucky bourbons opens with a vanilla and toffee-heavy nose that’s backed up by cherry candies and sweet tea. Baked goods and cinnamon bread lead on the palate. Despite the low proof, there’s some depth here, with buttered popcorn, cherry cola, and lemon candies lingering more faintly in the background. The finish is on the shorter side but delivers toasted oak, vanilla, and more cinnamon.

n: 1792 Cognac Cask Finished, 47.5%
t: This newcomer to the 1792 lineup (introduced to the market last September) has an alluring aroma of stewed
f: This newcomer to the 1792 lineup (introduced to the market last September) has an alluring aroma of stewed peaches. Peanut butter and freshly baked sourdough bread play on the palate, combining to create an inviting flavor, and while the finish is long, it has some grip to it. Water brings out herbal tea, roasted nuts, and orange marmalade. This is a tasty, if not game-changing whiskey.

n: Johnnie Walker Red Label, 40%
t: The entry-level blend in this range should never be overlooked. Sweet grain, honey, peanut brittle, vanilla
f: The entry-level blend in this range should never be overlooked. Sweet grain, honey, peanut brittle, vanilla cream, dried apple, and a green herbal note that suggests a higher grain content than other Johnnie Walker expressions. The palate has a thick, creamy mouthfeel, with vanilla, honey, peanut, and light spices, adding mandarin, green apple, and creamed coconut. Worth revisiting for an everyday pour as well as mixing.

n: Calistoga Depot Prosperous & Penniless Buena Vista Cabernet Sauvignon Wine Finished Malted Rye Malt (Batch No.1), 44.6%
t: This mash of malted rye and wheat aged in new oak for 24-30 months, then transferred to cognac casks, and
f: This mash of malted rye and wheat aged in new oak for 24-30 months, then transferred to cognac casks, and finished in California cabernet barrels. On the nose, this leads with sweet grape jelly, berry compote, and vanilla fudge. The palate is citrusy with lemon zest and grapefruit juice, but the grape and berry flavors remain strong. The finish is soft and subtle, with gentle spice finding balance with red fruits and grape must.

n: Rieger Sweet Mash, 45%
t: Despite a mashbill of 96% rye, this whiskey is a gentle example of American rye. On the nose, there’s sweet
f: Despite a mashbill of 96% rye, this whiskey is a gentle example of American rye. On the nose, there’s sweet cornbread dusted with pepper, sweet and spicy cinnamon candies, and a whisper of mint. The palate is similarly tame, with chai, vanilla, and Mexican hot chocolate. The whiskey is well-balanced and maybe just a little too tame; the flavors and aromas are cohesive but light. The finish follows suit with gentle pepperiness and milk chocolate.

n: Tenmile Distillery Revolutionary Whisky Series Battle of Stony Point, 46%
t: A 5 year old New York single malt aged in bourbon barrels and French oak pinot noir casks. The nose offers
f: A 5 year old New York single malt aged in bourbon barrels and French oak pinot noir casks. The nose offers dried stone fruits, fresh peach and apricot, and applesauce, joined by sweet chocolate and fudge. It has a light palate of chocolate, caramel, cherry, peach, marzipan, and orange. The chocolate carries over to the finish, joined by honey-roasted nuts and vanilla.

n: Castle & Key Small Batch 6 year old, 50.5%
t: This fruity, frisky bourbon, now a part of Castle & Key’s permanent lineup, kicks off with dried pineapple,
f: This fruity, frisky bourbon, now a part of Castle & Key’s permanent lineup, kicks off with dried pineapple, candied orange, vanilla bean, Creamsicle, and a trace of lilies on the nose. There’s some wood up front on the palate, but notes of single-origin coffee, açai, and cassis soon smooth it out. The finish turns darker, as dark-roast coffee, semi-sweet chocolate chips, Heath bar, and lemon peel take over.

n: First Call, 45%
t: A budget-friendly rye from Kentucky-based IJW Whiskey Co., a non-distiller producer, with a brand name
f: A budget-friendly rye from Kentucky-based IJW Whiskey Co., a non-distiller producer, with a brand name inspired by the bugle’s “first call” in thoroughbred racing. Drying oak with marshmallow and cassis notes start things off on a balanced and pleasant nose. A bright palate offers cherry sweetness, coconut flakes, bright red berries, and pepper spice. Cherry and dark chocolate tart dessert flavors complete a long finish. Nice flavors from a solid, straightforward whiskey.

n: High Wire Distilling Co. Jimmy Red Double Oak, 53.5%
t: Charleston, South Carolina-based High Wire’s take on a double oaked whiskey involved finishing its flagship
f: Charleston, South Carolina-based High Wire’s take on a double oaked whiskey involved finishing its flagship 100% Jimmy Red corn bourbon in new oak for 14 months. All of that virgin oak pops on the nose, which is drenched with caramelized sugar, vanilla pound cake, and wood spice. Lighter notes of apricot marmalade and raisin follow on the palate, mixing with baking spice, cinnamon syrup, and toasted nuts. A lot of wood, in the form of oak spice and barrel char, is present on the pleasant finish.

n: New Riff Winter Whiskey Bottled in Bond Malted Oat and Chocolate Malt, 50%
t: Made from a mash of 65% corn, 20% malted oats, 7% pale ale malt, 5% steel-cut raw oats, and 3% chocolate
f: Made from a mash of 65% corn, 20% malted oats, 7% pale ale malt, 5% steel-cut raw oats, and 3% chocolate malt, this leans heavily into stout beer notes. Dried and roasted grain on the nose gives way to faint caramel and vanilla. On the palate, while the whiskey remains dry and leads with that roasted grain, there are also subtle herbal flavors of mint tea and licorice. The finish is long with more stout and a hint of malted milk balls.

n: Remus Gatsby Reserve 15 year old Cask Strength (2025 Edition), 51.4%
t: Made at Ross & Squibb Distillery in Indiana, this ultra-aged bourbon offers a very aromatic nose of cocktail
f: Made at Ross & Squibb Distillery in Indiana, this ultra-aged bourbon offers a very aromatic nose of cocktail cherries, butterscotch, Werther’s Original, and malted chocolate milkshake. The palate has oak, more cherry, chocolate, bruised apple, and berry-flavored cough syrup. The finish adds leather, with the chocolate growing darker and more bitter.

n: Widow Jane Decadence Maple Syrup Barrel Finished Blend of Straights, 45.5%
t: On the nose, the barrel finish is evident, with prominent aromas of maple syrup, vanilla, and toasted oak
f: On the nose, the barrel finish is evident, with prominent aromas of maple syrup, vanilla, and toasted oak overpowering more delicate notes of sugar cookies, peach candies, and cinnamon sugar. The palate is rich, with strong maple flavors somewhat balanced by toasted oak, barrel char, and honey. The flavors imparted by the finishing barrel are dominant, letting up slightly on the finish, which shows cocoa, chicory, and more maple syrup.

n: Bobby Garg Family Reserve, 51%
t: The namesake label of Bobby Garg, a U.S. importer of Indian spirits, including Rampur whisky, is made at an
f: The namesake label of Bobby Garg, a U.S. importer of Indian spirits, including Rampur whisky, is made at an undisclosed Kentucky distillery from a mashbill of 74% corn, 18% rye, and 8% malted barley. The nose is dry but pleasant, with lots of ginger root, gingersnaps, oak, sassafras, candied jalapeños, and a bit of chocolate. Vanilla cookie batter, brownies, cola, and peppery heat all make an appearance on the palate. The finish adds grape jelly, oak, and chocolate chips.

n: Ampersand Vinea Kentucky Straight Rye & Cognac-Cask Aged Grain Spirit Blend, 46%
t: This new expression from Chip Tate is a blend of rye whiskey and 8 year old grain neutral spirits aged in
f: This new expression from Chip Tate is a blend of rye whiskey and 8 year old grain neutral spirits aged in cognac casks. It has a very odd nose of brown apple cores, honeydew, sugar, and mint. It’s thin on the palate, with some cognac cask-derived flavors like salted almonds, overripe fruit, and spice. The finish carries honey, spiced fruits, and oak. Lots of delicious flavors, but better integration would help.

n: Wigle Whiskey Reserve 4 year old Mezcal & Sherry Cask Finished, 46%
t: This Pennsylvania rye leads with an attractive nose of soft baking spices, cinnamon sugar, glazed apple
f: This Pennsylvania rye leads with an attractive nose of soft baking spices, cinnamon sugar, glazed apple doughnut, baked orchard fruit, applewood, and fruit tarts. The palate is similar, with the apple influence morphing into an almost cider-like flavor, joined by dry spices like nutmeg, cocoa, cumin, sassafras, kola nut, and oak. Some of those spices continue to the finish, joining with ginger, galangal root, orange, and cola.

n: Ampersand Malus American Rye Whiskey and Apple Brandy Blend, 46%
t: Another esoteric experiment from Chip Tate, this time blending 51% rye whiskey and 49% calvados, a French
f: Another esoteric experiment from Chip Tate, this time blending 51% rye whiskey and 49% calvados, a French apple brandy. Apple is the focus here, showing up as cider and baked apple doughnuts on the nose, and Apple Jacks cereal on the palate. The finish adds a bit of spice with cracked pepper, cinnamon, and oak. The calvados completely drowns out the rye, resulting in a one-dimensional blend that, while appealing to brandy lovers, might turn off whiskey aficionados.

n: Old Potrero California Cellar Series No. 03 Toasted Barrel Gundlach Bundschu Gewurztraminer Finished, 57.3%
t: Aged in new toasted oak for 5 years and 8 months, then finished for 14 months in Sonoma gewürztraminer dry
f: Aged in new toasted oak for 5 years and 8 months, then finished for 14 months in Sonoma gewürztraminer dry white wine casks. The nose is bright and lightly spiced, with cranberry, gingerbread, lychee, and bergamot. Bready and yeasty flavors emerge on the palate, including toasted grain and bran muffins, joined by dried fruits and citrus. The finish is a bit tastier, with snickerdoodle, gingerbread, and lemon zest. Interesting flavors that could be better integrated.

n: Willett Family Estate Small Batch 4 year old Cask Strength, 63.7%
t: Dry and waxy on a closed nose, with faint aromas of honey, lemon, and butterscotch poking through. Lots of
f: Dry and waxy on a closed nose, with faint aromas of honey, lemon, and butterscotch poking through. Lots of heat on the palate—water unlocks some honeyed sweetness, orange peel, vanilla, brown sugar, and tobacco. Still quite dry and spiky, with perhaps too much oak. The finish is vastly better in texture and balance, with sweet flavors of vanilla and red berries, and jalapeño spice. The potential is there, and can be tasted on the finish.

n: Chivas Brothers 12 year old, 40%
t: Matured in bourbon and sherry casks, this uses a recipe with Strathisla as a key malt. The nose has juicy
f: Matured in bourbon and sherry casks, this uses a recipe with Strathisla as a key malt. The nose has juicy orange, satsuma peel, honey, and vanilla, with hints of green apple and white pepper. Light-textured on the palate, with plenty of fresh citrus, caramel, dried apricot, tart shells, and vanilla sponge; it dives into candied orange at the swallow, with toffee and orange peel on the finish.

n: Redbreast Lustau, 46%
t: This is aged for 9-12 years, then finished for a year in first-fill Spanish oak oloroso sherry butts from
f: This is aged for 9-12 years, then finished for a year in first-fill Spanish oak oloroso sherry butts from Bodegas Lustau. The nose has plenty of depth, with baked apple, dates, leather, raspberry jam, cinnamon stick, black licorice, and dunnage earth. Well-rounded flavors of baked citrus, honey, peppery spices, clove, red velvet cake, damson, glacé cherry, and walnut, before it spirals down into a delicious sherry fruit abyss.

n: Malloy Hall Peated, 43%
t: Henley, Sebastian, and Prestige malt varieties are peated to 45 PPM, a level similar to Laphroaig’s malt,
f: Henley, Sebastian, and Prestige malt varieties are peated to 45 PPM, a level similar to Laphroaig’s malt, creating a nose of lemon mousse, citrus peel, mandarin, and bonfire smoke. It’s tasty, with honey, lemon sherbet, and ground black pepper, plus peat smoke pulsing in the background. A beautiful gingersnap note comes in later, ushering in a long finish of peat smoke and gingerbread.

n: Hinterhaus Singularity Port Cask Finish Cask Strength (Batch 1), 54%
t: The nose is rich and opulent, with jammy blackberries and strawberries, and cherry cordials. Toasted walnuts,
f: The nose is rich and opulent, with jammy blackberries and strawberries, and cherry cordials. Toasted walnuts, brownie batter, and a hint of amaretto are more subtle on the nose, but round out the fruit-forward aroma. The palate shows raisins, dried apricots, cinnamon stick, baking chocolate, and brown sugar. The finish lasts long and reveals baked apples, more raisins, and slightly bitter chocolate, with a turn toward confectioners sugar as it fades.

n: ImpEx Collection Spirit of Yorkshire 2018 Cask No. 3152, 52.7%
t: Buttery, malty, and attractive on the nose, with vanilla frosting, orange hard candy, white pepper, wood
f: Buttery, malty, and attractive on the nose, with vanilla frosting, orange hard candy, white pepper, wood spice, citrus peel, and incense, this makes for a rather wonderful olfactory experience. Dried apple, honey, malt, marmalade, and pepperiness to taste, hitting its stride with a pronounced candied ginger note before diluting to show warm mandarin, toasted pastry, and apricot jam, then concluding with sweet citrus and lasting spices.

n: Filey Bay Virgin Oak Cask 2018 Cask No. 3020, 60.1%
t: Distilled at Spirit of Yorkshire Distillery, the aromas show sanded oak, ice cream wafers, peppercorn,
f: Distilled at Spirit of Yorkshire Distillery, the aromas show sanded oak, ice cream wafers, peppercorn, candied orange, ground hazelnut, and banana chip. The high proof delivers a sustained blast of peppery heat at full strength, supported by flavors of maple syrup, walnut, orange peel, and that wafer note, with hints of root vegetable savoriness and oak tannins at the end. Water coaxes out milk chocolate and singed orange peels.

n: MilHòc Le Premier-Né Single Grain, 45%
t: Milhóc is making whisky in France’s Armagnac region. This, its debut release, is made from corn and malted
f: Milhóc is making whisky in France’s Armagnac region. This, its debut release, is made from corn and malted barley and aged in new oak, bourbon, and armagnac casks. The nose is bright and zippy, with aromas of lemon peel, lemon pound cake, a dollop of honey, and a faint soapy note. The palate is light but not thin, with lovely baking spices, café au lait, black pepper, and semi-sweet chocolate. Coffee intensifies on the finish, as does the peppery spice.

n: Yamazaki 25 year old Mizunara 2025 Release, 48%
t: Compared to the 18 year old, the mizunara aromas are deeper, sweeter, and more mature, with elevated notes of
f: Compared to the 18 year old, the mizunara aromas are deeper, sweeter, and more mature, with elevated notes of burning incense, grated nutmeg on panna cotta, apricot clafoutis, polished wood, and cardamom-sprinkled milk custard. Rich white chocolate, sweetened milk, clove-studded bitter orange, and kumquat flavors, with greater aged oak character adding sophisticated mature nuances to this experiential whisky. Truly nothing else like it.

n: Yamazaki 18 year old Mizunara 2025 Release, 48%
t: The mizunara aromas are bright and creamy compared to the 25 year old, with sandalwood, drifting incense,
f: The mizunara aromas are bright and creamy compared to the 25 year old, with sandalwood, drifting incense, cinnamon, leather, and a range of fruity notes: dried cherry, cranberry, and blueberry. Multiple flavor phases alternate between creamy vanilla custard and candied citrus on the palate, then cinnamon, nutmeg, ground pepper, and incense, before fruit notes of red cherry and goji berry emerge, leaving a satisfying finish of cherry and creamy latte.

n: Barrell Triple Rum Cask Jamaican, Barbados, & St. Lucian Rum Cask Finished, 71.2%,
t: Possibly the world’s first “hazmat” rum-fin- ished whiskey, and it delivers big on flavor. Rum sweetness,
f: Possibly the world’s first “hazmat” rum-fin- ished whiskey, and it delivers big on flavor. Rum sweetness, brown sugar, rice pudding and honey on the very fragrant and balanced nose. Richly sweet on the palate, and it holds the proof remarkably well, with melon, honey, and honeyed toast. The finish is long, sweet, flavorful, and balanced by ashy dry oak and pepper spice. Amazingly fresh and flavor packed at such a powerful proof.

n: Octomore 5 year old (16.3 Edition), 61.6%
t: Smoke and salinity simmer from the start, though aromas of sweet barbecue, nougat, simple syrup, orange peel,
f: Smoke and salinity simmer from the start, though aromas of sweet barbecue, nougat, simple syrup, orange peel, and a little must swirl about in equal parts. If the nose is a pencil drawing of flavor to come, the palate opens up into an oil painting—vivid notes of char, fig, black pepper, and Gala apple abound. Cassis, raisin, dark chocolate, orange oil, and soft ashy smoke make for an enchanting finish.

n: Elijah Craig 11 year & 6 month Barrel Proof (Batch B525), 63.1%
t: This batch was a true standout, benefiting from a longer aging period than its recent predeces- sors. It’s
f: This batch was a true standout, benefiting from a longer aging period than its recent predeces- sors. It’s powerfully proofed, as usual, but carries it well, offering flavors of raspberry tart, bitter chocolate, cinnamon, camp coffee, and balanced pepper spice. A long finish continues this great ride to the end, with the darker flavors punctuated by some vanilla sweetness, all balanced perfectly by the oak.

n: Gordon & MacPhail Artistry in Oak 85 year old Distilled at Glenlivet Distillery, 43.7%
t: Matured in a first-fill American oak sherry butt since 1940, this remarkable whisky is a spirit that defies
f: Matured in a first-fill American oak sherry butt since 1940, this remarkable whisky is a spirit that defies its age. Apricot, dried pineapple, citrus, antique wood, beeswax, and aromas of worn leather upholstery in vintage cars. Sweet tropical and orchard fruit flavors lead to vanilla, red peppercorn, morello cherry, and plum, with cinnamon, oyster mushroom, oak char, aged balsamic vinegar, herbs, and spearmint. A light-textured herbal finish lingers delicately.

n: Dailuaine Marbled Treasures 21 year old, 54.8%
t: Fully matured in Spanish sherry casks, this Dailuaine is the standout of the 2025 Special Releases. Exquisite
f: Fully matured in Spanish sherry casks, this Dailuaine is the standout of the 2025 Special Releases. Exquisite aromas of vine fruit, marmalade peel, black cherry jam, walnut shells, espresso, new leather, Red Vines, and dark chocolate mingle with blueberry and charred oak. Luxuriously rich, with raspberry jam, moist gingerbread, dark marmalade, Fig Newton, sultana, and plum-walnut jam, with a long finish of ginger spices. Water reveals even greater depths.

n: Kilchoman 14 year old 20th Anniversary Cask Series 100% Islay Ex-Sherry Butt Matured, 55%
t: In celebration of its 20th anniversary, Islay’s Kilchoman Distillery released four distinct single malts,
f: In celebration of its 20th anniversary, Islay’s Kilchoman Distillery released four distinct single malts, each one a blend of five casks. On the nose, this one has notes of brown sugar, graham cracker, and dried fruit, with that classic Islay smoke enticingly entwined. The ashy palate calls to mind campfire coals and tobacco smoke, but there’s delicious dark chocolate and more dark dried fruit. The finish is lengthy and bursting with spice, meatloaf glaze, and, of course, that delicate sweet peat.

n: Parker’s Heritage Collection 11 year old (2025 Release), 61.25%
t: Peanuts, unbuttered popcorn, milk chocolate, chocolate frosting, vanilla, pipe tobacco, and sweet oak on a
f: Peanuts, unbuttered popcorn, milk chocolate, chocolate frosting, vanilla, pipe tobacco, and sweet oak on a complex and very inviting nose. A thick, rich mouthfeel—a bit hot but in control—with red berries, orange slices, chocolate, almond, coconut, baked cherries, and bitter espresso. The finish offers more red berries, veering toward rich dark chocolate. Great texture, delicious flavors, but perhaps somewhat dry on the back end. Best with a rock of ice.

n: Wild Turkey Master’s Keep Beacon, 59%
t: Sweet gobs of caramel, vanilla, and toffee on a soft, candy shop nose tempered by muted aged oak, worn
f: Sweet gobs of caramel, vanilla, and toffee on a soft, candy shop nose tempered by muted aged oak, worn leather, and a hint of tobacco leaf. The powerful palate offers jammy raspberry, followed by lively pepper spice and cigar box, while water brings out caramel and vanilla sweetness. A long finish intertwines earthiness and sweetness. It comes on a bit strong on the palate, but there’s no denying its sweet, flavorful, and beautifully aged complexity.

n: Little Book Chapter 9 “None For Granted” Blended Straights, 60.9%
t: This latest chapter in the series brings together 7, 8, and 11 year old bourbon with an 8 year old rye, with
f: This latest chapter in the series brings together 7, 8, and 11 year old bourbon with an 8 year old rye, with blender Freddie Noe aiming for the “founding flavors” of American whiskey. The nose is redolent with cinnamon, apples, blueberries, blackberries, and caramel. The palate is oakier, with barrel char adding depth to brown sugar, peach, and toffee flavors. The finish is long and luxurious, with more cinnamon, brown sugar, and toasted oak.

n: Bushmills 26 year old Crystal Malt, 46%
t: Crystal malt is a specialty brewing malt made by stewing and roasting green malt, which creates crystalized
f: Crystal malt is a specialty brewing malt made by stewing and roasting green malt, which creates crystalized sugars in each kernel. The nose has honey cake, baked lemon, baklava, apple ring, soft caramels, and gentle oak spice. Deliciously smooth and creamy with butterscotch, pear, roasted nut, peppercorn, clove, crème brûlée, and dark chocolate, followed by blackberry jelly, vanilla extract, and coffee on the palate. There’s supple oak, honey, and pear to finish.

n: Nikka From The Barrel Extra Marriage 40th Anniversary Limited Edition, 51.4%
t: Given an extra 3-month marrying period in oak at Nikka’s Tochigi Aging Cellar, this is gorgeous liquid with
f: Given an extra 3-month marrying period in oak at Nikka’s Tochigi Aging Cellar, this is gorgeous liquid with rich aromas of caramel, smoke, honeycomb, Reese’s peanut butter cups, lemongrass, fresh ginger, and a hint of peat bog. Baked citrus, toffee, zesty lemon, and honey flavors, it has more pungent peat smoke than the malt component, rounding out with malt, butterscotch, cocoa powder, and caramel popcorn.

n: Booker’s “By the Pond” 7 year old (Batch 2025-02), 63.25%
t: Somewhat closed at first on the nose, but the palate is very lively, with vanilla cream, caramel, baked
f: Somewhat closed at first on the nose, but the palate is very lively, with vanilla cream, caramel, baked raspberries, cola, and toffee, along with tobacco, balanced aged oak, and black pepper. It’s a hot one for sure, but the flavors still manage to assert themselves. The finish is where it all really shines, blending more vanilla cream, milk chocolate, aged sweet oak, balanced pepper spice, and warehouse earthiness.

n: Aberfeldy 15 year old Bolgheri Red Wine Cask Finish, 46%
t: Red wine casks can overpower, but here the balance is perfect. Finished for 2 years in Italian red wine casks
f: Red wine casks can overpower, but here the balance is perfect. Finished for 2 years in Italian red wine casks from Tuscany, the nose brims with blackberry, black cherry, ripe Victoria plum, dark chocolate, peppercorn, licorice, and black tea. Aberfeldy’s honeyed core shines through layers of chocolate, black cherry, clove, nutmeg, plum pudding, and gentle oak. A beautifully poised malt with a long, indulgent finish of chocolate-dipped dark fruits.

n: Hakushu Peated Malt 18 year old 2025 Release, 48%
t: Clean, pristine, and refreshing on the nose, with mint chocolate, freshly mown grass, charred oak, lemon
f: Clean, pristine, and refreshing on the nose, with mint chocolate, freshly mown grass, charred oak, lemon peel, lychee, apricot, floral notes, and wisps of smoke. The palate has apricot jam, mango, yuzu, and Fig Newton initially, with peat smoke barreling through beautifully at the higher proof. Layers of ripe fruit follow, bathed in acacia honey, with a finish of tropical fruits, wood spice, smoke, cacao, and charred stave.

n: Eagle Rare 12 year old, 47.5%
t: A new permanent fixture in the Eagle Rare lineup. Honey, clove, and whipped cream, anchored by earthy oak on
f: A new permanent fixture in the Eagle Rare lineup. Honey, clove, and whipped cream, anchored by earthy oak on a very aromatic nose. This has a velvety smooth and soft texture; a deliciously gooey palate of honeyed almonds, buttered French toast, raspberry jam, and a bite of pepper spice. Long and delicious on the finish of vanilla ice cream drizzled with honey. Good body, full-flavored, and delicious.
